title: Sentinel: added an 'unevaluable' status, made an erased audit chain a violation, and stopped the workflow rendering green with zero invariants evaluated
body: The instrument built because a wrong ranking shipped for six days could not distinguish 'checked and clean' from 'never looked'. SentinelCheckStatus was ok|violation only, so report.ts rendered every non-violation as PASS. verifyReviewChain filters `where chain_pos is not null`, so nulling the column emptied the set and the invariant returned 'chain is empty - trivially valid': ERASING the whole tamper-evident ledger scored greener than altering one row. And the dispatched workflow gated its run step on a guard, but a skipped step does not fail a job, so ubuntu-latest produced a green check with 0 of 11 invariants evaluated. Now: sentinelVerdict() is the ONE derivation read by evaluator, unreadable path and parser; countReviewAudit compares chained rows to the whole ledger; run.ts writes a schema-valid all-unevaluable report on the unreadable path (exit 2). Verified live: exit 2, verdict 'unevaluable', artifact written where the old code wrote nothing. STILL UNCOVERED: the money and law layers have zero invariants. Commit 821a107.

title: Time-travelling claim gate: `asOf()` under /zdroj, /overeni and the schránka
body:
## Summary
The store already keeps every superseded node and edge version (`kg_node_history` / `kg_edge_history`) and exposes `asOf()` time-travel reads, yet no reader-facing surface reads them: the gate can only say `moved` when the reader pastes the old value, the receipt shows one tense, and the schránka refuses to say how far a score moved because "the graph keeps no prior-value snapshots" — a sentence that stopped being true when the bitemporal layer landed.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T1 (As-of re-derivation: moved/gone claims shown with both sides from the bitemporal store); deck rank #1 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

Today: `lib/db/pglite/repositories/kg.ts:14-35` documents that every replaced version is appended to history with a half-open `[recorded_at, superseded_at)` span, `supersedeUpsertChunk` (`kg.ts:116-144`) is the ONE upsert path (`kg.ts:208`), and `asOf(at)` (`kg.ts:67`, `:388-438`) returns `listKgNodes` / `listKgEdges` / `kgNeighbours` at an instant. Grep over `features/**` and `lib/**` finds no consumer of `asOf` except `scripts/data-analysis/kg-repair-orphans.ts:14,81`. Meanwhile `features/schranka/recomputeFact.ts:97-101` and `:178-184` state the graph "NEUCHOVÁVÁ předchozí hodnoty skóre" and emit a magnitude-free row; `features/overeni/verdict.ts:341-354` and `:389-399` derive `moved` only from `det.pasted.value` / `retrievedAt` (a bare ref with no pasted element can never be `moved`); `features/shared/provenance/getReceiptData.ts:57-80` reads the current edge only and answers `gone` with no "last seen" instant. The gap: the platform holds the evidence to answer "what did this address say on date D, and when did it change" and answers "unknown" instead.

Built: a server-only `features/shared/provenance/getClaimHistory.ts` that decodes a claim ref (edge/node/figure subject) and reads the version spine from `kg_node_history` / `kg_edge_history` (diffing only the prop the claim's metric reads — a wholesale-replaced `props` blob changes for unrelated passes). `/zdroj/<ref>` renders a "verze záznamu" ledger (recorded_at, superseded_at, gate state per version) and a `gone` receipt states the instant the record left the graph. `/overeni?ref=…&k=YYYY-MM-DD` re-derives via `asOf(k)` and `moved` shows both sides with both dates from the store, not from the pasted element. The schránka `recompute` delta gains a per-MP magnitude ONLY where the person node's history carries a prior `contribution_score` under a uniform prior pass (else the current "size unknown" sentence stays — missing is not zero). `/denik` gets a `recompute` row kind per MP dated `superseded_at`.

## Flow
- Add `KgAsOfReads.getKgNodeVersions(id)` / `getKgEdgeVersions(src,rel,dst)` in `lib/db/pglite/repositories/kg.ts` (indexed on `kg_node_history_id_idx`, cap + `warnIfTruncated`).
- Pure `features/shared/provenance/claimHistory.ts`: version spine → per-metric value series; unit tests over a PGlite fixture that upserts twice (the `kg-bitemporal.test.ts` pattern).
- `/zdroj`: version ledger section; `gone` receipt cites `superseded_at`.
- `/overeni`: optional `k=` (as-of day) param; `figuraVerdict` gains `store`-sourced `citedValue`/`citedDate` when no element is pasted; three verdicts unchanged.
- `recomputeFact.ts`: read prior uniform pass from history via `summarizeContributionProvenance`; emit magnitude only under uniform prior; copy for the mixed case.
- `/denik` + feeds: `recompute` kind; `/schranka` `KIND_ORDER`/`KIND_NOUNS` extended in the same order.
- Docs: `docs/routes/{overeni,schranka,denik}.md` dated entries; memory note retiring "no prior snapshots".

## Expected impact
Journalists and MPs get "what changed and when" for any citation without keeping their own screenshots; the schránka's most-read delta stops hedging. Measured by the share of `/overeni` `moved` verdicts that carry a store-sourced date (today 0). Could break: history rows written by `clearKg --reset` (`kg.ts:333-377`) archive whole-graph rebuilds as one instant, so a version ledger must label a reset as "rebuild", not "change".

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a bare ref can be dated and diffed without the reader supplying the old value
Before: 0 features read `asOf`; `moved` requires `det.pasted` (`verdict.ts:389-391`); recompute delta magnitude = never (`recomputeFact.ts:99`)
After: MISSING INSTRUMENT — count of person-node history versions per MP on the live store (not measured; needs a read of `kg_node_history` grouped by id)
Method: probe - grep for `asOf(` consumers, read of the history DDL and the three refusing modules
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
evidence:
- `lib/db/pglite/ddl.ts:313-338` — `kg_node_history` / `kg_edge_history`, append-only, indexed by `(id, recorded_at desc)`
- `lib/db/pglite/repositories/kg.ts:67`, `:116-144`, `:208`, `:388-438` — `asOf()` exists and every upsert supersedes
- `features/schranka/recomputeFact.ts:97-101`, `:178-184` — "graf NEUCHOVÁVÁ předchozí hodnoty" → magnitude refused
- `features/overeni/verdict.ts:341-354`, `:389-399` — `moved` only from pasted value/derivation
- `features/shared/provenance/getReceiptData.ts:57-80` — current-only read, `gone` has no instant
- `MEMORY.md` → recompute-replay-gate: a formula correction must replay the old formula; history gives that gate an independent witness

title: Sealed instrument readings — the velín as a dated series, not a live-only view
body:
## Summary
Every chamber reading the velín and the landing publish exists only as "today's re-derivation": the store keeps no sealed reading per data release, so (a) a store outage still degrades to the invented sample (`buildStateGraph()`, `CHAMBER_STATS`, `CHAMBER_TREND`), (b) the platform cannot show a real time series of its own headline figures, and (c) a stale exhibit can only say "the hash differs", never what the cited page actually said.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T1 (As-of re-derivation: moved/gone claims shown with both sides from the bitemporal store); deck rank #2 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

Today `getDashboardData()` dates its output by the wall clock (`getDashboardData.ts:574` `builtOn = new Date()…`) and the page falls back to fiction when the loader is null: `DashboardPage.tsx:74` (`slice?.graph ?? buildStateGraph()` — invented MPs and firms), `:96` (`CHAMBER_TREND` — a fake six-quarter trend the file itself calls "no real analog"), `:421` (`MockStatTiles` over `lib/civic` `CHAMBER_STATS`), `:597` (`MockRankingLedger`). The landing refuses the mock (`LandingPage.tsx:16-17`, `:201-215`) but can only say "unavailable" — it has nothing dated to show instead. The exhibit (`exhibit.ts:195-197`) carries `urlHash`/`currentHash`/`fresh`; `ExhibitPage.tsx:254-257` renders a stale notice with two hashes, and `/overeni`'s `hashedVerdict` (`verdict.ts:198`) answers `moved` with only today's side — the registry's own technique says a `moved` verdict shows BOTH sides and both dates, which is impossible without the cited content.

Meanwhile the data layer already has the seal: `ingest_run.merkle_root` (`getAtlasData.ts:66-73`), a release `version`/`cutAt` (`features/data-releases/manifest.ts:46-51`), and a hash-chained ledger (`getDataReleasesData.ts` header). What is missing is a **reading table**: one row per data release holding the velín's projection (`DashboardData` minus `slice.sources`, i.e. exactly the `publicWire` shape), the landing's `LandingData`, the slice `graph`+`rule` and its `hashSlice`, and the release version that produced it — written by the same writer that cuts the release, never at request time.

"Built" looks like: (1) `/dashboard` renders today's re-derivation exactly as now, and when the store is down renders the LAST SEALED READING stamped "odečet z verze 2026.08.04 — úložiště momentálně nečitelné" in the ILLUSTRATIVE visual form the design already has (ochre edge), with the mock renderers deleted; (2) the histogram tile gains a real series — average index per release — replacing the fake `CHAMBER_TREND` with the one time series the platform can honestly claim; (3) `/dashboard/exponat/rez.<hash>` on a mismatch looks the hash up in the sealed readings and shows "what was cited (version V, date D) — what today derives (pass P, date D2)" side by side; the gate's `moved` verdict carries both.

## Flow
- Define `InstrumentReading` (pure, `features/dashboard/reading.ts`): `{releaseVersion, cutAt, pass, provenance, tiles, top, histogram, slice: Pick<StateSlice,"graph"|"rule">, sliceHash, landing: LandingData}` — the wire shapes, imported not copied; canonical JSON + `contentHash` for a reading fingerprint.
- Add `instrument_reading` table (additive DDL via `npm run db:migrate`; one writer repository, append-only, keyed by release version) and have the release-cutting path in `scripts/data-analysis` write one reading per successful `kg-compute`/`kg-promote` run, sealed into the ledger chain like `merkle_root`.
- Loader: `getLatestSealedReading()` (server-only, `react.cache`); `getDashboardData()` unchanged; `app/dashboard/page.tsx` passes `{live, sealed}` and `DashboardPage` renders live → sealed-labelled → `DataUnavailable`, in that order; delete `buildStateGraph()`/`MockStatTiles`/`MockRankingLedger`/`CHAMBER_TREND` consumers from the velín (the `lib/civic` shapes stay for tests until their last consumer goes).
- Landing: `SpecimenUnavailable` and the ranking section render the sealed reading with its version, using the same `LiveDataNotice` wording pattern ("stav k", "vysazeno" precedent from the referendum embed).
- Series: `histogram` tile gets `avgByRelease[]` from the reading table (every point cites its release version); `ChamberChart` draws it instead of the mock trend.
- Exhibit + gate: `getExhibitData()` on `fresh === false` queries readings by `sliceHash` = `urlHash`; `ExhibitViewModel` grows `cited: {version, cutAt, graph, rule} | null`; `hashedVerdict` `moved` carries both sides; `/overeni` prints both dates.
- Tests: reading fingerprint determinism, fallback order, `publicWire.test.ts` pinned shape equality, `freshness.test.ts` unchanged; a sealed reading is NEVER served as "today" (the label is asserted in `messages.test.ts`).

## Expected impact
Readers and citing newsrooms see a dated reading instead of a sample when the store is down, get the first honest time series of the index, and a stale citation shows what it said. Measured by: mock renderers referenced from `features/dashboard` → 0; exhibits answering `moved` that can show the cited side → from 0 to all whose hash exists in the reading table. What could break: a reading written from a half-recomputed store (`provenance.state !== "uniform"`) must be refused at write time or the series inherits the mixed-store lie.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality | resilience — the front door stops degrading to fiction and the platform gains a citable series of its own headline figures
Before: 4 mock renderers on the velín's fallback path (`DashboardPage.tsx:74,96,421,597`); 0 stored readings; `moved` verdicts carry one side (`verdict.ts:198`)
After: 0 mock renderers; N readings = N successful releases; `moved` carries both sides whenever the cited hash was ever sealed — MISSING INSTRUMENT today: nothing records what a page said at release time
Method: probe — read the fallback branches, the exhibit view model, the gate verdict, and the release/ledger seal path
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract — new table + new writer in the release path; DDL change goes through `db:migrate`
evidence:
- `features/dashboard/DashboardPage.tsx:74` `const graph = useMemo(() => slice?.graph ?? buildStateGraph(), [slice]);`
- `features/dashboard/DashboardPage.tsx:96` `CHAMBER_TREND.map(...)` — fallback trend; `lib/civic/data.ts:447` `CHAMBER_TREND = [54.2, …]`
- `features/dashboard/DashboardPage.tsx:421` `<MockStatTiles />`; `:597` `<MockRankingLedger />`; `components/MockStatTiles.tsx:9` imports `CHAMBER_STATS` from `lib/civic/data`
- `features/dashboard/getDashboardData.ts:574` `const builtOn = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);`
- `features/dashboard/exhibit.ts:195-197` `currentHash`, `fresh: boolean` — no cited content
- `features/dashboard/ExhibitPage.tsx:254-257` stale notice = two hashes
- `features/overeni/verdict.ts:198` `lookup.view.fresh ? verified : moved` — one side only
- `features/data-releases/manifest.ts:46-51` `version`/`cutAt` per release; `features/atlas/getAtlasData.ts:66-73` `merkle_root` sealed runs
- `features/landing/LandingPage.tsx:201-215` unavailable branch — nothing dated to render

title: Receipts for derived figures: `claim:` refs resolve at /zdroj with their inputs
body:
## Summary
The product has two claim grammars and only one of them has a receipt: a graph record (`h.`/`u.` → `/zdroj/<ref>`) gets a page showing provenance, gate and registries, while a derived FIGURE (`claim:<dataset>:<metric>:<subject>`, minted by `CitableNumber` in 12 files) can only be re-verified as a bare value at `/overeni` — nothing shows what rows it summed, under which formula, over which population.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T2 (A claim address on every figure: registry-keyed citations, figure receipts, exports and the machine gate); deck rank #3 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

`decodeClaimRef` (`features/shared/provenance/claimRef.ts:71-87`) accepts exactly `u.<b64>` and `h.<b64>.<b64>.<b64>`; a `claim:` ref answers `null` → 404. `getReceiptData` (`getReceiptData.ts:44-104`) reads one node or one edge + `review_audit`. The value-claim side lives in `lib/claims/claim.ts` (`Claim.derivation` at `:69`, `reviewStatus` `:55`) and is verified by `features/overeni/liveFigures.ts`, which forwards to the owning loaders (`getMoneyMpDetail`, `getCompanyDetail`, `getLeaderboardData`, `getLawData`; `:28-44`) and by `figuraVerdict` (`verdict.ts:104-121`) which compares value and derivation only. So when a newsroom pastes "23 653 407 340,55 Kč" the gate says verified/moved but cannot show the 1 000+ `supplies` edges, the `moneyReachesCompany` attribution rule (memory: supplies-is-not-attribution), the `KG_READ_CAP` that bounded the read, or the `pending_review` share of the ties underneath. That is the "footnote that outlives its number" failure mode: the value is re-derived, its derivation is not shown.

"Built" = `/zdroj/<claim-ref>` accepts the `claim:` family (refDetect already knows it: `refDetect.ts:7,66`) and renders a **figure receipt**: the value as today's loader mints it; `derivation` (`CONTRIBUTION_FORMULA_REF`, `kg-pass:N`) and the methodology link; the INPUT ROW SET as a capped, population-stated list (n edges of N, ordered by `byListOrder`, with the cap printed); the population's gate mix (verified / pending / rejected counts — the "uniform/mixed/absent" idea applied to the gate); and each input edge linking to its own `h.` receipt. The receipt is derived per request by the SAME owning loader (extend `IssuedFigure` with an optional `inputs: {rows, total, cap, gateMix}` that each loader fills from what it already read — `getMoneyMpDetail` already holds the ties; `getLeaderboardData` already holds the component inputs per MP). ClaimReview JSON-LD stays gated by `toClaimReviewJsonLd` (`receipt.ts:348-353`): a figure over a population with any non-verified input emits nothing.

## Flow
- Extend `ClaimRef` union with `{kind: "figure", ref: ClaimRefParts}` and teach `decodeClaimRef`/`encodeClaimRef` the `claim:` prefix (append-only: existing `h.`/`u.` addresses unchanged; pin in `claimRef.test.ts`).
- Add `FigureReceipt` to `receipt.ts` (`kind: "figure"`) with `value`, `unit`, `derivation`, `methodologyUrl`, `inputs` (capped list + `total` + `cap` + `gateMix`), `computedAt`; a pure `deriveFigureReceipt(issued: IssuedFigure)`.
- Extend `IssuedFigure` in `liveFigures.ts` with optional `inputs`; fill it in the money loaders first (ties are already in memory), then contribution (six components + committee seats), then law.
- `getReceiptData` routes `figure` refs through `liveFigures` (registry-then-live order preserved; store down → `unavailable`).
- `ReceiptBody` gains the figure layout: value, formula line, inputs table with population line, gate-mix line, link to `/overeni?ref=`.
- `CitableNumber` (`lib/claims/CitableNumber.tsx`) wraps the `<data>` in the `/zdroj/<ref>` link so the 12 files' figures become clickable receipts without per-site work.
- `liveFiguresRoundTrip.test.ts` grows: every metric constant must yield a receipt with `inputs.total ≥ inputs.rows.length` and a printed cap.

## Expected impact
A journalist quoting an MP total can open the sum and see the rows, the attribution rule and how much of it a human has confirmed; the `/overeni` `moved/basis` verdict finally has a page to point at for "what the basis is". Measured: number of metric families with a resolvable receipt (0 of 3 today → 3), and the share of figures whose receipt states its population and cap. What could break: the figure receipt is a heavier read than an edge receipt (a company reach can be ~784 edges) — it must reuse the loader's already-materialised rows, never issue a second `kgNeighbours` (memory: default limit 500 truncation).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality — a derived figure's receipt shows inputs, formula and gate mix, not only the value
Before: `/zdroj/claim:…` → `decodeClaimRef` returns null → 404 (`claimRef.ts:86`); `/overeni` verdict for figura carries `figure.value`, `citedValue`, `citedDerivation` only (`verdict.ts:57-79`); 12 files render `CitableNumber` with no receipt link
After: `/zdroj/<claim-ref>` renders a figure receipt for all metric constants enumerated by `liveFiguresRoundTrip.test.ts`; the round-trip test asserts population + cap are present
Method: probe — read `claimRef.ts` decoder, `getReceiptData.ts` branches, `verdict.ts` figura union, grep of `CitableNumber` consumers (12 files)
Result: better
Gate: contract — `ClaimRef` union and `IssuedFigure` grow additively; address space stays append-only
evidence:
- `features/shared/provenance/claimRef.ts:71-87` — only `u`/`h` prefixes decode; `:86 return null;`
- `features/shared/provenance/getReceiptData.ts:44-104` — node/edge only; `:67` `store.kgNeighbours({ id: ref.src, rels: [ref.rel], limit: KG_READ_CAP })`
- `features/overeni/refDetect.ts:7` "figura — claim-ref (`claim:<dataset>:<metric>[:<subject>]`, lib/claims)"; `:66` figura family
- `features/overeni/liveFigures.ts:11-12,28-44` — re-derivation through the owning loaders
- `features/overeni/verdict.ts:104-121` `figuraVerdict` compares `value` and `derivation`; no inputs
- `lib/claims/claim.ts:55,69` `reviewStatus?`, `derivation?`
- `CitableNumber` consumers: `features/money/{MpCaseFilePage,CompanyCaseFilePage,components/TiesLedger}.tsx`, `features/civicscore/{KrajPage,components/LeaderboardTable}.tsx`, `features/lawwatch/{StatuteDossierPage,components/BillDetail,components/ForensicIndexSection}.tsx`, `features/profile/components/MoneySection.tsx`, `features/overeni/OvereniPage.tsx`, `features/shared/components/AnimatedScore.tsx`, `app/svedectvi/page.tsx`
- `docs/routes/overeni.md` — "the MP total (23 570 594 009,66) and the company reach verify the same way, and all of them carry `pending` because all 211 ties do" — the gate mix exists as a fact, not on any receipt

title: Citation registry: every SourceNote keyed to a declared source with a live as-of
body:
## Summary
The brand rule is enforced as "a file contains a `<SourceNote>`" (lint) and the note's text is a free string — 427 call sites, 311 of them `t("…")` catalog strings, with "psp.cz" spelled 128 different ways in `messages/cs.json` and no join from any citation to the twelve declared sources in `lib/analysis/atlas.ts` or to `ingest_run.finished_at`. A citation therefore states a *cadence* ("denně", "7 dní") that is a promise, never the measured day the data actually holds.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T2 (A claim address on every figure: registry-keyed citations, figure receipts, exports and the machine gate); deck rank #4 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

Today `SourceNote` (`features/shared/components/SourceNote.tsx:83-95`) takes `children: ReactNode`, measures their length to pick label/sentence typography and renders them verbatim; the only structured hook is the opt-in `provenance?: ProvenanceReceipt` (`:81`), which is used by **0 of 427** call sites (measured by a node walk over `app/**` + `features/**`: total 427, withProv 0, t-calls 311, expressions 92, literals 24). The lint rule `packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/rules/require-source-citation.cjs` checks file-scoped *presence* of a satisfier element, not what it says. Meanwhile the store carries the truth the citation should print: `ingest_run(source, finished_at, source_last_modified, rows_written)` (`lib/db/pglite/ddl.ts:14-25`), the declared per-source cadence `SOURCE_CADENCE_DAYS` (`lib/analysis/atlas.ts:58-69`) and the atlas scorecard (`SOURCE_SPECS` at `:193-208`, consumed only by `features/atlas/getAtlasData.ts`, `features/landing/components/DataSources.tsx`, `app/atlas/atlas.json/route.ts`). The gap: the citation and the freshness/quality record are two systems that never meet, so the same source can score "zastaralé" on `/atlas` while every `SourceNote` on `/hlasovani` still reads "psp.cz — jmenovitá hlasování, denně".

"Built" = a `lib/sources/registry.ts` (pure, one definition) declaring each source id from `SOURCE_SPECS` with its proper name, registry host, license note and cadence key; a server-side `sourceStamps()` read (one `ingest_run` query per request, `react.cache`d) returning `{sourceId → {asOf, runStatus, staleness}}`; a `<SourceNote source="psp-hlasovani" …>` form that renders the declared name + the MEASURED as-of ("stav k 28. 8. 2026") and, when `stalenessOf()` says stale, carries the ochre form marker the same way `StatTile variant="illustrative"` does (`StatTile.tsx:39-45`) — the staleness must survive a skim, not just a caption. Unknown source id → the note renders the literal and a `bez registru` badge, never silently. The lint rule grows a second trigger: a `SourceNote` whose text names a host that exists in the registry but carries no `source=` is a warning that ratchets like `require-source-citation` did. The 12 atlas cards and every citation then cite ONE vocabulary, and `/atlas` becomes the place a reader lands from any citation (card link = `/atlas#<sourceId>`).

## Flow
- Extract `SOURCE_SPECS` + `SOURCE_CADENCE_DAYS` into `lib/sources/registry.ts`; `lib/analysis/atlas.ts` imports them (no behaviour change; pinned by existing atlas tests).
- Add `sourceStamps()` server loader (`lib/db/`-level, `reportLoaderFailure` on null) reading the latest `finished` `ingest_run` per source; expose through the page-level loaders' props (the `/hlasovani` template pattern), NOT via a client fetch.
- Extend `SourceNote` additively: `source?: SourceId`, `stamp?: SourceStamp | null`; when both present render "‹name› · stav k ‹date›" and the stale form marker; `stamp === null` renders "‹name› · stav neznámý" (missing is not zero).
- Migrate the 311 catalog citations by source family (votes → money → law → budget), replacing free-text hosts with `source=`; keep the descriptive tail ("jmenovitá hlasování") as `children`.
- Add the lint trigger (`custom/require-source-registry`) at `warn` under `features/**`, measured count published in `eslint.config.mjs` like the 11 citation violations were.
- `/atlas` cards get stable anchors; every stamped citation links to its card.

## Expected impact
Readers and newsrooms see on every figure the day the underlying dataset was last ingested, not the day the page rendered; the sentinel's freshness finding (`lib/testing/sentinel/invariants.ts` header, "zastaralé") stops being a hidden operator fact and reaches the citation. Measured by the count of citations carrying a measured as-of (0 today) and by the number of distinct host spellings in `messages/cs.json` (≥15 for psp.cz today → 1). What could break: a `SourceNote` string change touches ~240 files of snapshot/i18n parity tests (`messages.test.ts` per feature) — the migration must be per-family with the cs/en key-parity tests as the gate.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality — a citation states a measured as-of instead of a declared cadence
Before: 427 SourceNote sites, 0 with structured provenance, 0 joined to `ingest_run`; "psp.cz" appears in 128 catalog strings in ≥15 spellings; `/atlas` freshness is reachable only from `/atlas` and the landing panel
After: every migrated citation carries `source=` + as-of; the MISSING INSTRUMENT is a lint count for citations-without-registry-key (analogous to the burned-down `require-source-citation` count)
Method: probe — node walk over all `.tsx` in `app/`+`features/` counting `<SourceNote>` forms; grep of `messages/cs.json`; read of atlas.ts specs and ddl
Result: better

title: One audited review door for every claim kind, not just money ties
body:
## Summary
The repo has exactly ONE human review door (`setTieReviewState` on `linked_to` edges, audit-chained) while three other machine-produced claim kinds — bill forensic verdicts, tripwire candidates, money web-leads — have no writer at all, so their `pending_review` is permanent by construction and nothing can ever promote, reject or even record a human look at them.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T3 (One audited review door for every claim kind (bill verdicts, effort verdicts, identity, corrections, exposure)); deck rank #5 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

Today: `lib/db/pglite/repositories/review.ts:1,22,48` is "the human-review write path for `linked_to` ties" — the only writer of review state and the only appender to the tamper-evident chain (`ledger.ts:3`); `review_audit` itself is tie-shaped (`lib/db/pglite/ddl.ts:253-265`: `src/rel/dst`, decision in `confirm|reject|needs-more`). Bill forensic verdicts are written `pending_review` by `kg-forensics.ts` (`lib/analysis/law-verdict.ts:12-14`) and read by `features/lawwatch/getLawData.ts:292,340`, which even DEFAULTS an absent state to `"pending_review"` — grep shows no writer of `forensic_review_state` anywhere outside the triage readers (`scripts/case-loops/law/triage-core.ts:206`). `/zakony` prints `pending_review · 141` beside an "ungated" note (`ForensicIndexSection.tsx:21-27`): the review console for bills is a sentence, not a door. Tripwire candidates are "KANDIDÁT PRO LIDSKOU REVIZI, nikdy zjištění" (`lib/analysis/tripwires.ts:9-15`) and deep-link to `/penize/kontrola#tie-…` (`TripwireSection.tsx:24,79`) — but an operator who examines one and finds nothing can record NOTHING, so the same candidate returns on every read (`tripwires.ts:6-7`: derived per read, no state). Money leads (`getAdminData.ts:456-481`) are JSON payloads on disk with no state at all. The one append-only operator journal that exists, `driveLog`, admits it is "VLASTNÍ řetěz žurnálu — Merkle pečeť revizního ledgeru se na ně NEVZTAHUJE" (`driveState.ts:12-16`). The registry's human-review-doors technique is explicit: one code path is the only writer of review state, audit-append then update in one transaction, reject terminal, and "if a surface renders a model's interpretation about a person to the public, it takes the door" — 141 bill verdicts render on `/zakony` today with no door.

Built: `review_audit` generalised to a claim-kind discriminator (`subject_kind: tie | bill_verdict | tripwire | lead`, subject id = the existing stable address — edge triple, `bill:tisk:N`, `tripwireCandidateId`, `leadId`) with ONE `setReviewState(subject, decision, reviewer, note)` writer that appends the chained audit row and then applies the subject-specific prop write (edge props for ties, `forensic_review_state` for bills, a `tripwire_review` prop on the tie edge keyed by candidate id, a lead sidecar). The sentinel's `audit-chain` check then covers all four populations by construction. `/admin`'s "Fronta revize" becomes a real queue (population + decided/pending per kind), `/zakony` shows a verified/rejected verdict the way `/penize` shows a tie, and `/overeni` receipts for bill claims carry a gate state that can actually change.

## Flow
- Add `subject_kind` + generic `subject_id` columns to `review_audit` via `npm run db:migrate` (additive; existing tie rows backfilled as `tie` with their triple — no chain rewrite, prior hashes untouched, new rows hash the wider payload under a new domain tag `politicas-audit-v2`)
- Extract the transaction skeleton of `setTieReviewState` into a `ReviewRepository.setReviewState()` dispatcher; ties keep their exact write; add `bill_verdict` (writes `forensic_review_state` + history row), `tripwire` (records look/dismiss/escalate against the candidate id — a dismissal is a decision, not a deletion), `lead`
- Reviewer identity: reuse `REVIEWER_TOKEN` (kontrola) for ties and bills; `ADMIN_TOKEN` operator for tripwires/leads; both go through the same door, never a second endpoint
- Sentinel: `audit-chain` reads `ReviewAuditCounts` per kind and ships the four populations; add `review-coverage` check = for each kind, pending / decided / total (never a rate without its denominator)
- Surfaces: `/admin` ReviewHubSection turns its four read-only counters into queues with decision buttons (same two-phase confirm pattern as `LoopMissionControl`); `/zakony` BillDetail shows the gate state from the store instead of the defaulted string; `getLawData.ts:340` stops defaulting to `pending_review` — an absent state renders as absent
- `gateVocabulary.ts` grows the bill/tripwire kinds; `/overeni` verdict for a bill claim carries the modifier; ClaimReview JSON-LD stays gated on `verified` only
- Tests: chain verifies across mixed kinds; reject is terminal per kind; a tripwire dismissal is invalidated when the candidate's evidence fingerprint changes (same rule as `loopState` alert acks, `loopState.ts:217-219`)

## Expected impact
Reviewers get one queue over four claim kinds instead of one door plus three permanent "pending" labels; readers of `/zakony` see verdicts that can actually be confirmed or refused; the sentinel's chain finally vouches for every machine claim that reaches a reader. Measured by: number of claim kinds with a writer (1 → 4) and the fraction of rendered `pending_review` labels that can change. What could break: the `review_audit` hash preimage — must be a new domain tag, never an edit of the old rows.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality — every reader-facing machine claim gains an auditable human decision path
Before: 1 review writer (`review.ts:48`), 211/211 ties pending, 141/141 bill verdicts pending with no writer, tripwire candidates re-derived with zero recorded dispositions
After: 4 claim kinds behind one chained writer; `/admin` queue shows decided/pending/total per kind; sentinel `audit-chain` covers all four
Method: probe — grep for writers of `forensic_review_state` (0 outside triage readers), read `review.ts`, `ddl.ts`, `tripwires.ts`, `TripwireSection.tsx`
Result: better
Gate: irreversible
evidence:
- `lib/db/pglite/repositories/review.ts:1` "the human-review write path for `linked_to` ties"; `:22` `const LINKED_TO = "linked_to"`; `:48` `setTieReviewState(src, dst, decision, reviewer, note)`
- `lib/db/pglite/ddl.ts:253-265` review_audit shape is `src, rel, dst, decision check in ('confirm','reject','needs-more')`
- `lib/analysis/law-verdict.ts:12-14` "Findings that pass are written pending_review — a lead for a human, never a published verdict."
- `features/lawwatch/getLawData.ts:340` `reviewState: state ?? "pending_review"`; `scripts/case-loops/law/triage-core.ts:206` is the only other reader; no writer found
- `features/lawwatch/components/ForensicIndexSection.tsx:21-27` the `pending_review · 141` line next to the ungated note
- `lib/analysis/tripwires.ts:6-7` "NIC SE NEZAPISUJE — kandidáti se odvozují znovu při každém čtení"; `:9-15` candidate-not-finding discipline
- `features/admin/components/TripwireSection.tsx:24,79` links out to `/penize/kontrola#tie-…`, no local action
- `features/admin/loops/driveState.ts:12-16` the operator journal's own admission that the Merkle ledger does not cover it
- `features/admin/getAdminData.ts:456-481` leads read from `payloads/batch-*-lead-*.json`, no state

title: Published correction ledger: the right of reply as a hash-chained record
body:
## Summary
A named MP or firm who believes a politicas figure is wrong has a `mailto:` link that renders only when an env var is set, and the platform records nothing about the complaint or its outcome; the only chained, public decision log is `review_audit`, which covers tie confirmations and nothing else. The ethics standard the repo subscribes to names a published correction history as a duty — it does not exist.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T3 (One audited review door for every claim kind (bill verdicts, effort verdicts, identity, corrections, exposure)); deck rank #6 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

Today: `features/shared/components/ReportClaimLink.tsx:11-14`, `:33-34` — env-gated `mailto:` composed on click, no server-side trace; `lib/db/pglite/ddl.ts:253-262` — `review_audit` is the sole append-only log (decision ∈ confirm/reject/needs-more over an edge triple), chained by `lib/db/pglite/repositories/review.ts:96-116` under the `politicas-audit-v1` domain (`lib/db/pglite/ledger.ts:5-7`, `:22-27`: a serialization change "requires a new domain-separation tag, never an edit"); `features/dukazy/deriveFeed.ts:85` — the public bulletin knows `"tie" | "forensic"` entries only; `/zdroj` and `/overeni` have no notion of "this address has a filed correction". The `recompute-invalidates-prose` and `recompute-replay-gate` memories describe corrections that DID happen (pass 42 moved 33 scores, 30 dossier sentences stale) with no public record of them beyond route docs.

Built: a `correction` table in the same tamper-evident ledger (own domain tag `politicas-correction-v1`, `chain_pos`/`prev_hash`/`row_hash`), one row per adjudicated report: the claim ref (decoded and refused on mismatch, the `edgeClaimRef` precedent), `kind` ∈ `withdrawn | corrected | upheld`, the value before/after or null, the reason, who decided, `decided_at`, and a pointer to the incident doc. Written ONLY from `/admin` (the existing ADMIN_TOKEN lane) — a reader's report becomes a `lens`-style anonymous submission (`ddl.ts:375-384` pattern: no identity), queued for the same human gate. Renders: `/dukazy` gains a `correction` entry kind and the feeds carry it; `/denik` a `correction` row keyed by the claim's entities; `/schranka` a `correction` delta ("a claim about a followed entity was corrected"); `/zdroj/<ref>` a banner above the receipt with the chained row; `/overeni` a verdict MODIFIER (never a fourth verdict): "adresa nese opravu ze dne D"; `/data` prints the correction chain head beside the review chain head. `upheld` renders with the same weight as `corrected` — a contested-and-held figure is a finding too.

## Flow
- `db:migrate`: `correction` + `correction_report` tables; `ledger.ts` new domain tag + `verifyCorrectionChain` (pure, reused by `/data`'s integrity read).
- `lib/db/pglite/repositories/corrections.ts` — the ONLY writer; PGlite test writes two rows and verifies the chain (the `chainRow.test.ts` pattern).
- `/admin`: report queue + decision form; `ReportClaimLink` posts the report (server action, no identity, `mailto:` kept as fallback when the store is down).
- `features/dukazy/deriveFeed.ts`: `correction` kind; `readReviewAudit.ts` sibling `readCorrections.ts` with cap + `truncated`.
- `/denik`, `/schranka` kinds + vocabularies in shared order; `/zdroj` banner; `verdict.ts` modifier field + copy keys in both catalogs through the language gate.
- `/data`: manifest `integrity.correctionChain`; `feedIndex` note.
- Docs: `docs/routes/{dukazy→denik,schranka,overeni,data}.md`; incident anchor per correction in `docs/`.

## Expected impact
A named subject can contest a figure and see the outcome published at the claim's own address; readers who cited it are notified through the inbox they already use. Measured by corrections filed vs adjudicated per month and by the count of `/zdroj` receipts carrying a chained correction (today 0, and unmeasurable). Could break: a correction that changes a stored value must go through the recompute replay gate — the ledger records the decision; it never edits the graph itself.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every published correction has a permanent, chained, machine-checkable address
Before: 0 correction records anywhere; the contest route is `mailto:` gated on `NEXT_PUBLIC_CONTACT_EMAIL` (`ReportClaimLink.tsx:33-34`); the bulletin knows two entry kinds (`deriveFeed.ts:85`)
After: MISSING INSTRUMENT — the count of corrections historically warranted (pass-42: 33 moved scores, 30 stale sentences per MEMORY) vs the count publicly recorded (0)
Method: probe - read of ReportClaimLink, review_audit DDL + chain writer, ledger domain contract, dukazy entry kinds, MEMORY incident notes
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: irreversible
evidence:
- `features/shared/components/ReportClaimLink.tsx:11-14`, `:33-34`, `:36-46` — env-gated `mailto:`, nothing recorded
- `lib/db/pglite/ddl.ts:253-262` — `review_audit` decisions limited to edge triples
- `lib/db/pglite/repositories/review.ts:96-116` — chain append lives only here
- `lib/db/pglite/ledger.ts:5-7`, `:22-27` — versioned domain tags; new domain, never an edit
- `lib/db/pglite/ddl.ts:375-384` — `lens_submission`: the identity-free submission precedent
- `features/dukazy/deriveFeed.ts:85` — `kind: "tie" | "forensic"`
- `MEMORY.md` → recompute-invalidates-prose, recompute-replay-gate — corrections occurred with no public ledger

title: Chamber readings as a claim family — every velín tile citable, resolved live
body:
## Summary
The four figures the velín makes the largest on the page — chamber attendance mean (with its population), attributable CZK, the forensic counts, the average index — mint no claim-ref; and the one chamber figure the claim registry DOES know ("prumerna-dochazka") resolves against the `lib/civic` sample tile dated 2026-07-30, which the gate consults BEFORE the live store, so a pasted attendance citation is verified against a mock.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T2 (A claim address on every figure: registry-keyed citations, figure receipts, exports and the machine gate); deck rank #7 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

`lib/claims/registry.ts:22-23` imports `CHAMBER_STATS` / `CHAMBER_SUMMARY` from `lib/civic`; `:50` `SAMPLE_RETRIEVED_AT = "2026-07-30"`; `:87-106` mints `prumerna-dochazka` from the mock tile string via `czechTileNumber`, `issuedAt: "/svedectvi"`. `features/overeni/liveFigures.ts:66-70` limits live resolution to `MONEY_CLAIM_DATASET`, `SCORE_CLAIM_DATASET`, `LAW_CLAIM_DATASET`, and `docs/routes/overeni.md:13-15` states the order is registry-then-live. The velín's real readings are computed in `getDashboardData.ts:532-542` (attendance mean over `counted`/`total`, nulls excluded) and projected from owners (`moneyHeadline` `:303-322`, `lawHeadline` `:343-356`), yet `grep CitableNumber features/dashboard` returns nothing — no tile is a claim. `MONEY_METRIC` (`liveFigures.ts:95-102`) has per-MP and per-company metrics but no chamber total; `LandingPage.tsx:135-141` mints only the per-MP composite; `HeroStory` prints `count` and the hemicycle from `scores` with a SourceNote and no ref.

"Built": `features/dashboard/readingClaims.ts` (pure; the `scoreClaim.ts` discipline) mints chamber-wide claims — `psp.cz — omluvy : prumerna-dochazka` (value + `population: counted/total` in the claim body), `registr smluv ⋈ ares : pripsatelne-kc` (with `isFloor` as a modifier, never a different number), `lawwatch : forenzni-posudky`, `psp.cz — příspěvkový index : prumerny-index` — each with `derivation` from the POPULATION aggregate (`provenance.state === "uniform"` → `ref@pass`, else omitted, per the technique). Tiles render through `<CitableNumber>`; `liveFigures.ts` resolves them by calling `getDashboardData()` (the owner); the registry's sample attendance figure is retired (or its dataset renamed so it can never shadow a live one), and `/overeni` verifies the front door's numbers against the front door's loader. The same pure module feeds `GET /dashboard/odecet.json`: the chamber reading as `{claims[], derivation, population, builtOn}` — the first concrete endpoint of the "API pro redakce".

## Flow
- `readingClaims.ts` + test: metric slugs, dataset constants imported from the owners' vocabularies (`COMPONENT_DEFS` source string for omluvy, `MONEY_CLAIM_DATASET`, `LAW_CLAIM_DATASET`, `SCORE_CLAIM_DATASET`); `readingDerivation(provenance)` reuses `scoreDerivation`.
- `DashboardPage.tsx` stat tiles + `HeroStory` count: wrap the numeral in `<CitableNumber claim=…>`; the money tile passes `isFloor` as claim modifier text, not into the value.
- `liveFigures.ts`: add the chamber datasets to `LIVE_DATASETS`; resolvers call `getDashboardData()` (already `react.cache`-adjacent via the memoized money layer); `gone` when the population is empty; `unavailable` when the store is down.
- `lib/claims/registry.ts`: drop the mock-derived `prumerna-dochazka` (keep the constitutional 200 and the `/svedectvi` sample under a dataset name that says "vzorek"); `overeni.md` and `guide.ts` example updated.
- `app/dashboard/odecet.json/route.ts`: serialises `readingClaims(getDashboardData())` with `Cache-Control` bound to `MONEY_MEMO_TTL_MS`; listed on `/data`'s feed address book (`feedIndex.ts`).
- `messages.test.ts` (dashboard) pins that every tile with a numeral carries a claim; `liveFiguresRoundTrip.test.ts` gains the four chamber refs.

## Expected impact
Newsrooms quoting "průměrná docházka 87,3 %" get a permanent address that re-derives from the omluvy register with its population, and the gate stops confirming a mock; the velín's four numerals become `verified`/`moved` answers instead of unaddressable. Measured by: claim-bearing numerals on `/dashboard` 0 → 4 (+1 on `/`); registry figures resolving from `lib/civic` 3 → 1. What could break: a chamber claim minted while `provenance.state === "mixed"` must ship without derivation — the pure module has to refuse to invent one.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality — the highest-traffic figures gain provenance addresses, and the verification gate stops answering from sample data for a chamber metric
Before: `grep -c CitableNumber features/dashboard/**` = 0; `resolveClaimRef("claim:<CHAMBER_STATS attendance source>:prumerna-dochazka")` returns the mock value dated 2026-07-30 (`registry.ts:87-106`)
After: 4 tiles + landing count minted; the same ref resolves through `getDashboardData()` with `population {counted,total}` — instrument: `liveFiguresRoundTrip.test.ts` mint → bare ref → verified with identical value
Method: probe — grep for claim primitives in the group, read the registry and the live resolver's dataset set
Result: better (the shadowing is reproducible from the registry order alone)
Gate: none

title: Verification as a protocol: machine verdicts, JSON receipts and whole-article au
body:
## Summary
The Civic Claim Gate answers one pasted ref with an HTML page; a newsroom that quotes twelve politicas figures in one article has no way to re-check them together, and no machine can ask the gate anything — `/data` lists three machine endpoints and none of them verifies.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T2 (A claim address on every figure: registry-keyed citations, figure receipts, exports and the machine gate); deck rank #8 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

Today: `app/overeni/page.tsx:21-28` reads a single `?ref=` string; `ls app/overeni app/zdroj/[ref]` shows `page.tsx` only — no `route.ts` under either; `features/data-releases/feedIndex.ts:83-99` enumerates `MACHINE_ENDPOINTS` (novinky, manifest, snapshot) with no verification address; `features/overeni/refDetect.ts` classifies one URL (`detectAt` unwraps our own `?ref=` at depth 1). The three-verdict vocabulary, the gate-as-modifier (`verdict.ts:522-526`) and the derivation comparison are all pure and key-returning already (`docs/routes/overeni.md` "Standing rules") — the protocol exists as functions and is missing its wire.

Built: (1) `/overeni.json?ref=…` (and `/zdroj/<ref>.json`) — the same `getVerdictData` / `getReceiptData` serialised: `{ verdict: verified|moved|unknown, gate: verified|pending|rejected|ungated, value, derivation, citedValue, citedDate, receipt: "/zdroj/…", schemaVersion }`, `Cache-Control` per the feed precedent, 503 on an unreadable store (never an empty frame). (2) A batch mode: `POST /overeni.json` with up to `AUDIT_REFS_CAP` refs (or a pasted article body from which `refDetect` extracts every politicas address and `data-claim-*` element) → one verdict per ref plus the cap and the count dropped; the HTML `/overeni` gains the same textarea and a verdict table. (3) `feedIndex.ts` lists both endpoints as machine endpoints; `/data` prints them. ClaimReview JSON-LD stays gated at the emitter — the batch API returns the gate state as a field, never as review markup.

## Flow
- `features/overeni/wire.ts`: pure serializer from `GateVerdict` → JSON (message KEYS, not sentences — the consumer localises), pinned by a test that walks `VERDICT_COPY_KEYS`.
- `app/overeni.json/route.ts` (GET single, POST batch) + `app/zdroj/[ref].json/route.ts`, sharing the loaders; per-request `cache()` dedupes repeated refs in one article.
- `refDetect.ts`: `detectAll(text)` over a document — every URL and every `data-claim-ref` attribute; count of non-citation URLs reported, never silently dropped.
- `OvereniPage.tsx`: document mode; verdict table; each row links its receipt.
- `feedIndex.ts` + `feedIndex.test.ts` (asserts the routes exist in `app/`); `/data` copy.
- Docs: `docs/routes/{overeni,data}.md`; `memory/` note on batch cost.

## Expected impact
Editors re-verify an article in one request before print, and CMS plugins can auto-check a draft; measured by batch requests per week and by the ratio of `moved` verdicts caught before publication. Could break: each ref costs a loader call (~806 ms cold for the guide example); an uncapped batch is a DoS — the cap ships its population and the 429 path is part of the design.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a newsroom can verify N claims in one request, by machine
Before: 1 ref per request, HTML only (`app/overeni/page.tsx:24-28`); 0 verification endpoints in `MACHINE_ENDPOINTS` (`feedIndex.ts:83-99`)
After: MISSING INSTRUMENT — p95 latency of a 12-ref batch on the live store (no batch exists to time)
Method: probe - directory listing of `app/overeni` / `app/zdroj/[ref]`, read of the route, feedIndex and verdict modules
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
evidence:
- `app/overeni/page.tsx:21-28` — single `ref` search param, HTML page
- `app/overeni/`, `app/zdroj/[ref]/` — `page.tsx` only, no `route.ts`
- `features/data-releases/feedIndex.ts:83-99` — three machine endpoints, none verifying
- `features/overeni/verdict.ts:306`, `:522-526` — closed vocabulary and gate tone already pure
- `features/overeni/getVerdictData.ts:34-104` — family router reusable by a JSON route unchanged
- `docs/ROADMAP.md` "Next" §3 — "API pro redakce" named, undesigned

title: Record-time citations: every receipt re-derives at the instant it was cited
body:
## Summary
The store already keeps every superseded version of every kg claim and exposes `asOf()`, but the API is not in the `Store` contract, has one script consumer, and no citation surface can show what the graph said WHEN the reader cited it — a `moved` verdict today shows only today's side.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T1 (As-of re-derivation: moved/gone claims shown with both sides from the bitemporal store); deck rank #9 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

`lib/db/pglite/repositories/kg.ts:53-66` declares `BitemporalKnowledgeGraphRepository.asOf()` and says it is "deliberately declared HERE, not in lib/db/store.ts … later batches can lift it into the Store interface" and "an un-indexed union of serving + history tables — a history instrument, not a hot serving path". `lib/db/store.ts:171-195` (`KnowledgeGraphRepository`) carries no `asOf`; the only non-test caller is `scripts/data-analysis/kg-repair-orphans.ts:14,81`. Meanwhile the write side is complete: `supersedeUpsertChunk` (kg.ts:107-150) and the review flip (`review.ts:131-146`) archive every prior version with a contiguous `[recorded_at, superseded_at)` span, and `review.ts:136-140` states that "this tie sat in pending_review for 4 months" is "a queryable fact" — yet nothing queries it.

On the citation side, `lib/claims/claim.ts:51` already stamps `retrievedAt` (day precision) and `:57-69` the `derivation`; `/overeni` (`features/overeni/liveFigures.ts`) re-derives against TODAY only, and `docs/routes/overeni.md` records the vocabulary as `verified | moved | unknown` with `moved` carrying one side. The registry technique requires `moved` to show "both sides and both dates"; the repo cannot, because no read path asks the store for the cited instant.

Built: (1) `asOf` lifted into `Store` with an explicit contract ("record time; before the bitemporal epoch answers `unknown`, never a value"); (2) `kg_edge_history_key_idx` / `kg_node_history_id_idx` (ddl.ts:325,339) promoted to the serving path for point reads — a single-key `asOf` read via those indexes is cheap even if the whole-relation union is not; (3) `getReceiptData.ts:65-67` (today `kgNeighbours` on the serving table) gains a second leg: when the pasted claim carries `retrievedAt`, the receipt also renders the version visible at that instant, and `verdict.ts` compares cited-instant vs today and prints both values, both `review_state`s and both `provenance.pass` stamps; (4) the `/zdroj` receipt gains a "review standing over time" strip from `kg_edge_history` joined to `review_audit` (the 4-months fact); (5) `retrievedAt` upgraded to an instant on newly minted claims (the day-precision field stays decodable — append-only address space).

## Flow
- Lift `asOf` into `KnowledgeGraphRepository` (`lib/db/store.ts`) with the epoch rule as a typed result (`{ known: false, epoch }`), not a silent fallback to serving rows.
- Add a point-read `asOfClaim({src,rel,dst}, at)` / `asOfNode(id, at)` that uses the history key indexes (measure on the 2 GB copy; the union lister is not the path).
- Extend `Claim` with `retrievedAtInstant` (append-only key order, claim.ts:71-90) and mint it from every live figure (`liveFigures.ts`, `moneyClaims.ts`, `scoreClaim.ts`).
- `getReceiptData` + `verdict.ts`: two-sided `moved` (value, basis, review_state each compared), with both dates; a cited instant before the epoch reports "record time unknown before <epoch>" and compares nothing.
- `/graf/p/[ref]`: the second fingerprint (`docs/routes/graf-permalink.md` "both fingerprints") becomes a re-derived as-of fingerprint, not a stored one.
- Pin with `kg-bitemporal.test.ts` extensions + `liveFiguresRoundTrip.test.ts` (mint → advance store → `moved` with both sides).

## Expected impact
A journalist who cited a tie in July and re-verifies in September sees "then: pending_review, 23,65 mld.; now: rejected, 23,65 mld." instead of a bare `moved`; measured as the share of `moved` verdicts that render both sides (0 today). The epoch boundary (all pre-migration rows share one `recorded_at`, `changes.ts:19-24`) is the thing that could break honesty — it must render as unknown, never as "unchanged since 2026-08".

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a `moved` verdict becomes a two-sided, dated statement instead of a one-sided one
Before: `asOf` has 0 feature consumers (grep across features/app: only `scripts/data-analysis/kg-repair-orphans.ts`); `moved` in `features/overeni/verdict.ts` carries today's value only; 211/211 `linked_to` ties `pending_review` (overeni.md) so the review-over-time strip would currently show one span each
After: every claim minted with an instant re-derives two-sided; the instrument is a count of `moved` verdicts with `both sides present` in the gate's own test suite
Method: probe - read kg.ts/store.ts/claim.ts/getReceiptData.ts, grep for consumers
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence:
- `lib/db/pglite/repositories/kg.ts:53-66` — `asOf` declared outside the Store contract, "not a hot serving path"
- `lib/db/store.ts:171-195` — `KnowledgeGraphRepository` without `asOf`
- `lib/db/pglite/repositories/review.ts:131-146` — flip supersedes; "4 months in pending_review" called queryable, unqueried
- `lib/db/pglite/ddl.ts:288-339` — bitemporal columns + history tables + key indexes
- `lib/claims/claim.ts:51,57-69` — `retrievedAt` (day) and `derivation` already on the claim
- `features/shared/provenance/getReceiptData.ts:65-67` — receipt reads serving table only
- `lib/db/pglite/repositories/changes.ts:19-24` — the shared-epoch caveat

title: Temporal receipts: /zdroj and the gate answer "as of the day you cited it"
body:
## Summary
The store is bitemporal (`kg_node_history`, `kg_edge_history`, `review_audit` hash chain) and the repository exposes `asOf(at)` — but no reader-facing path reads it: a `moved` verdict shows today's side only, and a `gone` receipt shows the decoded address plus whatever endpoints survive, never the last recorded version of the edge.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T1 (As-of re-derivation: moved/gone claims shown with both sides from the bitemporal store); deck rank #10 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

`lib/db/pglite/ddl.ts:300-335` adds `recorded_at`/`superseded_at` to `kg_node`/`kg_edge` and the append-only `kg_node_history`/`kg_edge_history`; `lib/db/pglite/repositories/kg.ts:58-68` declares `BitemporalKnowledgeGraphRepository.asOf(at)` ("the graph as it was known at `at`"). `grep -rn "\.asOf(" features app lib` outside tests/repositories → **0 hits**. `getReceiptData.ts:70-81` on a missing edge returns `gone` with `toDecodedClaim` over the current nodes; the header comment calls this "the WORST moment for the reader". `figuraVerdict` (`verdict.ts:104-121`) and the zdroj/graf verdicts carry `citedDate` but never query the store at that date: `moved` is "today differs from what you pasted", with no statement of what the platform itself published on `citedDate`. The registry says a moved claim must show both sides and both dates; today one side is the reader's paste.

"Built" = (1) the claim address family gains an optional `k=<YYYY-MM-DD>` (as-of) query on `/zdroj/<ref>` and `/overeni?ref=&k=`: the receipt is re-derived through `store.asOf(k)` and typeset with a dated banner ABOVE the content (the `/graf/p` staleness rule, `docs/routes/graf-permalink.md`), both fingerprints shown; (2) a `gone` receipt additionally reads the last history version (`kg_edge_history` newest by `recorded_at`) and renders it as "naposledy zaznamenáno … / nahrazeno …" — disclosed as history, never re-promoted to a current claim; (3) `moved` verdicts (zdroj and figura where `citedDate` is present) fetch the platform's own value at `citedDate` and print three columns: cited by reader · published by us on that day · today. Where the history has no row spanning `citedDate` (store predates history), the column says "záznam k tomu dni neexistuje" (missing is not zero). Every change surfaced this way already has a `change_event` twin (`ddl.ts:343-356`, writer `repositories/changes.ts`) — the receipt links the events between the two dates so `/denik` becomes the narrative of why the claim moved.

## Flow
- Add `asOf` reads to `getReceiptData` behind a validated `k` param (ISO day only; anything else is refused, not repaired — the `forensicMode.ts` "adresa je tvrzení" discipline).
- Index `kg_edge_history(src, rel, dst, recorded_at desc)` is already there (`ddl.ts:340`); add a `lastVersion(src, rel, dst)` repository read for `gone`.
- `receipt.ts`: `ProvenanceReceipt` gains `asOf: string | null` and `history: {recordedAt, supersededAt} | null`; `ReceiptBody` posts the dated banner above the content.
- `verdict.ts`: `moved` variants gain `publishedAtCitedDate: {value | receipt, recordedAt} | null`; pure, tested with fixture history rows.
- `/denik` link: `change_event` rows between `citedDate` and today for the claim's `src`/`dst` keys, capped with the cap printed.
- `docs/routes/overeni.md` + `graf-permalink.md` dated record entries.

## Expected impact
A reader defending a screenshot from June can prove what the platform said in June; a subject contesting a tie can see when it changed and which gate decision changed it. Measured: `moved` verdicts that show both sides (0 today → all where history spans the date), `gone` receipts that show a last version (0 → all with a history row). What could break: `asOf` runs over an un-indexed union (kg.ts:64-65) — must be bounded to the single claim key, never a neighbourhood, or the receipt page becomes a slow path.

## Evaluation
Claim: user — a moved/gone claim shows what the platform published on the cited day
Before: `asOf` has 0 reader-facing consumers; `gone` = decoded address + surviving endpoints (`getReceiptData.ts:70-81`); `moved` = pasted value vs today (`verdict.ts:107-121`), `citedDate` carried but unused for lookup
After: the same three cases render the dated side; the MISSING INSTRUMENT is a history-coverage count (share of current edges that have ≥1 history row) to state when "no record for that day" is the honest answer
Method: probe — grep for `.asOf(` consumers; read ddl history tables, repository interface, receipt loader and verdict
Result: better
Gate: contract — new optional query param on issued addresses; address space unchanged
evidence:
- `lib/db/pglite/ddl.ts:300-335` bitemporal columns + `kg_node_history`/`kg_edge_history`; `:340` `kg_edge_history_key_idx(src, rel, dst, recorded_at desc)`
- `lib/db/pglite/repositories/kg.ts:58-68` `asOf(at: Date | string): KgAsOfReads` — "a history instrument, not a hot serving path"
- `grep -rn "\.asOf(" features app lib | grep -v test | grep -v repositories/` → no output
- `features/shared/provenance/getReceiptData.ts:40,61,70-81` the `gone` arm
- `features/overeni/verdict.ts:57-79` `moved` carries `citedValue`, `citedDate`, `citedDerivation` — nothing read at `citedDate`
- `lib/db/pglite/ddl.ts:343-356` `change_event` "derived from the bitemporal kg history + review_audit"
- registry: three-verdict-vocabulary — "moved … shown with both sides and both dates"

title: Claim-ref ratchet: the lint doctrine moves from "a citation somewhere in the fil
body:
## Summary
`require-source-citation` is satisfied by ONE `<SourceNote>` anywhere in a file (120 files), while the machine-verifiable form — a `CitableNumber` with a claim ref the `/overeni` gate can re-derive — exists on 19 files and a registry of three chamber figures; the brand rule is enforced at file granularity and verifiable at figure granularity, and nothing ratchets one toward the other.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T2 (A claim address on every figure: registry-keyed citations, figure receipts, exports and the machine gate); deck rank #11 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

Today: `packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/rules/require-source-citation.cjs:29-58` — "What satisfies the rule … FILE-scoped: any of these anywhere in the same file: a provenance element … `data-undisclosed` … `// citation-ok`", and `:219-226` clears every candidate the moment `fileSatisfied` is true. So a file with twelve figures and one caption is clean, and no rule can say WHICH figure the caption covers. The addressable form exists and is well-built: `lib/claims/claim.ts:36-70` (ref, dataset, metric, subject, derivation, reviewStatus), `claimDataAttributes` (`:140-157`) emits `data-claim-*` on the DOM, `lib/claims/registry.ts:112` holds `ISSUED_FIGURES` — three figures — and `features/overeni/liveFigures.ts:89-94` routes a handful of metrics to the loaders that own them. `/overeni` (`docs/routes/overeni.md`) therefore verifies money ties, company figures, leaderboard scores, law census — and answers `politicas-neni-citace` for every other number on the site, which is most of them (120 SourceNote files vs 19 CitableNumber files). The registry's claim-ref-addressing technique is that the address carries the claim's identity so the server can re-derive from the address alone; today a reader who pastes `/rozpocty`, `/hlasovani` discipline, `/volby` ledger figures or `/dashboard` tiles gets "our page, not a citation".

Built: a second doctrine rule, `require-claim-ref`, in the plugin: a formatter call in JSX child position must be a `<CitableNumber claim={…}>` (or sit inside an element carrying `data-claim-ref`) — same triggers as `require-source-citation` (`:9-27`), satisfier per FIGURE not per file, `// claim-ok: <reason>` for the genuinely un-addressable (an index, a column count). Ships at `warn` with a measured inventory written into `eslint.config.mjs` exactly the way the two existing ratchets did (`eslint.config.mjs:86-135`), then graduates route by route as each feature's numbers get a metric in `liveFigures.ts` — `liveFiguresRoundTrip.test.ts` already fails on a metric without a routing branch, so a claim ref can never be minted without a re-derivation path. `lib/claims/registry.ts` stops being a hand list: `ISSUED_FIGURES` is derived from each feature's `*Claims.ts` module (the `lawClaims.ts` precedent) so the finite registry and the live router share one declaration. The `/overeni` gate then accepts any figure on the site, and the `SourceNote` primitive stays as the human caption — the two are complementary, not competing.

## Flow
- Write `rules/require-claim-ref.cjs` + RuleTester suite mirroring `require-source-citation`'s trigger set; satisfier = enclosing `CitableNumber` or `data-claim-ref` on the nearest JSX ancestor; `claim-ok` opt-out with a reason
- Measure: `eslint --format json` repo-wide, record the count per file in the config comment (the ratchet convention), ship at `warn` under `features/**`, `error` under `app/**` if measured zero there
- `lib/claims/registry.ts`: `ISSUED_FIGURES = [...civicscoreClaims, ...lawClaims, ...moneyClaims, ...]` with a test that every ref parses, is unique, and routes in `liveFigures.ts`
- Per route (order by reader traffic: `/zebricek`, `/poslanec`, `/hlasovani`, `/rozpocty`, `/volby`, `/dashboard`): add a `<feature>Claims.ts` with `makeClaimRef({dataset, metric, subject})` per figure, wrap the render in `CitableNumber`, add the loader branch to `liveFigures.ts`, flip the route's severity to `error`
- `/overeni` `refDetect`: recognise `data-claim-ref` pasted from any page (already does), and the `politicas-neni-citace` reason shrinks as routes graduate — its count is the burn-down metric, printed on `/data`'s feed address book as "citovatelné plochy N z M"
- `no-source-note-size-override` precedent: the citation primitive owns its legibility; `CitableNumber` gets the same rule

## Expected impact
A journalist can paste ANY number from the site into `/overeni` and get `verified | moved | unknown`, not "not a citation"; the brand rule gains a per-figure machine check that cannot be satisfied by a caption three sections away. Measured by: `require-claim-ref` warning count (unknown today; the rule is the instrument) and the share of public routes whose figures route in `liveFigures.ts` (today ~4 families of ~16 routes). What could break: a claim ref minted without a re-derivation path — prevented by the round-trip test; and DOM weight from `data-claim-*` on dense tables (measure on `/zebricek`).

## Evaluation
Claim: user — every rendered figure becomes independently re-derivable by address
Before: `require-source-citation` satisfier is file-scoped (`:219-226`); 120 SourceNote files vs 19 CitableNumber files; `ISSUED_FIGURES` = 3 registry figures; `/overeni` answers `politicas-neni-citace` for most routes
After: per-figure rule with a printed inventory that only goes down; registry derived from feature claim modules; `/overeni` coverage printed as N of M routes
Method: probe — read the rule, `claim.ts`, `registry.ts`, `liveFigures.ts`; `grep -rl CitableNumber` (19) vs `grep -rl "<SourceNote"` (120)
Result: unmeasurable (the count the rule would produce does not exist until the rule does)
Gate: policy
evidence:
- `packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/rules/require-source-citation.cjs:29-58` file-scoped satisfiers; `:219-226` `if (fileSatisfied) return;`
- `lib/claims/claim.ts:36-70` the claim shape incl. `derivation`; `:140-157` `claimDataAttributes`
- `lib/claims/registry.ts:59,76,95,112` three issued figures
- `features/overeni/liveFigures.ts:89-94` metric router; `docs/routes/overeni.md` "A metric added without a routing branch FAILS `liveFiguresRoundTrip.test.ts`" and the `politicas-neni-citace` reason
- `grep -rl CitableNumber app features lib` → 19 files; `grep -rl "<SourceNote" app features` → 120 files
- `eslint.config.mjs:86-135` the two ratchets' measured-inventory convention this rule would follow
- `app/svedectvi/page.tsx:10-16` "Široká adopce (žebříček, spisy) je práce pozdějších dávek" — the adoption was deferred in 2026-07 and never scheduled

title: One review lane for person-level verdicts — effort claims get the money layer's
body:
## Summary
Every effort-loop verdict about a named person — low-score reason (34/207), workhorse (≈16/207), rapporteur load, tenure class, public-role prose — is a model-authored, deterministically-gated claim rendered on /zebricek rows, /kraj posters and /poslanec with a date but no review state, no human gate and no audit chain, while the money layer's 211 ties get all three.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T3 (One audited review door for every claim kind (bill verdicts, effort verdicts, identity, corrections, exposure)); deck rank #12 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

`readChamber()` reads `effort_low_score_reason`, `effort_workhorse`, `effort_workhorse_flavour`, `effort_rapporteur_load` straight off the node (`features/civicscore/getLeaderboardData.ts:569-577`) and the profile reads the prose fields the same way (`features/profile/getProfileData.ts:538-558`, behind `publicCopyOrNull` only). `LowScoreReasonChip` renders vocabulary copy plus `recordedAt` (`LowScoreReasonChip.tsx:52`); `WorkhorseBadge` renders the claim, the turn count and the date (`WorkhorseBadge.tsx:66-67`) — nothing says whether a person or a pipeline decided it. The vocabulary already carries a per-reason tone (`lib/analysis/low-score-reason.ts:53-54, 90`) and the golden-path technique requires the reason to be „stored as a separate reviewable fact with pending-review provenance… that a human gates" and „each assignment carries who or what asserted it". The writers are `scripts/case-loops/effort/gate.ts` (deterministic gate, no human decision recorded — `grep human|reviewer` over `merge-batch.ts`/`finalize-ledger.ts` → 0) and the props are stamped `effort_provenance{computedAt}` only. The money layer, by contrast, has `ClaimReviewStatus` (`lib/claims/claim.ts:33`), a review console, a tamper-evident `review_audit` chain and sentinel coverage — and the sentinel record itself notes that layers outside contribution have ZERO invariants (`docs/routes/zebricek.md:159-164`); the effort layer is one of them.

"Built" = effort verdicts become claims on the ladder: (1) each `effort_*` verdict prop gains `review_state ∈ {machine, verified, rejected}` + `decided_by/at` inside `effort_provenance` (prop-registry extension), written `machine` by the loop; (2) the review console (`/penize/kontrola`'s pattern) gains a „Verdikty o poslancích" lane over the same `review_audit` chain — decisions append to the chain, rejections withhold the badge; (3) every badge renders its rung: „strojově odvozeno" vs „ověřeno (kdo, kdy)", through one shared `VerdictProvenance` primitive in `features/shared/components/` (catalog); the `Claim` shape (`ungated`) is reused where a figure is minted; (4) sentinel invariants `effort-review-chain` (every non-machine verdict has an audit row) and `effort-vocabulary` (every stored reason is in `LOW_SCORE_REASONS`) — turning the effort layer from unobservable to checked; (5) symmetry: the console orders by evidence completeness, never by score or party, and the verified-negative („genuine_absentee") sits in the same lane with the same weight.

## Flow
- Extend `lib/kg/prop-registry.json` and the effort writers (`gate.ts`, `merge-batch.ts`) to stamp `review_state: "machine"` on every effort verdict; backfill the 207 nodes merge-preservingly on a copy with a full props diff.
- `lib/analysis/verdict-provenance.ts` (pure): read state + decider off `effort_provenance`; `rungKey()` → message keys; tests pin the language gate.
- Review console lane: `lib/db/pglite/repositories/review.ts` gains a subject kind for `psp:person:<id>` × `effort_*` field; `review_audit` chain unchanged in shape (the tamper-evidence invariant covers it for free).
- Render: `LowScoreReasonChip`, `WorkhorseBadge`, `RapporteurBadge`, `DossierSection` prose, Souboj — one primitive, both densities, poster footer via `posterProvenanceNote()`.
- Sentinel: two invariants above; `facts.ts` collects effort provenance; `sentinel.test.ts` proves a mass `machine → verified` flip without audit rows fires.
- /metodika: a §"Verdikty" line stating the rung vocabulary and the gate.
- Docs: `zebricek.md`, `poslanec.md`, `penize.md` (console), `analysis-quality` notes.

## Expected impact
Readers see which rung each person-level badge stands on; a cited MP can contest a verdict through the same console that already exists for ties; the effort layer stops being the one claim class about named people that no invariant watches. Measured by: badges carrying a rung (0 → all), effort verdicts with a review row (0 → N decided), sentinel invariants over `effort_*` (0 → 2). Could break: badge density on /zebricek rows — the rung label must not push `LeaderboardRow` past its compact grid; and a `rejected` verdict must withhold, never blank a row to „no reason" (the honest empty state is „verdikt zamítnut", disclosed).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality — rung inflation made structurally impossible for the person-level verdicts
Before: `grep -rn "review_state\|reviewStatus" features/civicscore features/profile lib/analysis/low-score-reason.ts lib/analysis/workhorse-flavour.ts` → 0; 34 low-score chips + ≈16 workhorse badges + 18 rapporteur badges render dated but ungated; 0 sentinel invariants over `effort_*`
After: every rendered verdict carries `machine|verified|rejected` + decider; a fault-injected flip without audit rows is a sentinel violation; count of undated-or-unranged verdicts = 0
Method: probe — read both loaders' prop reads and both badge components; grepped the effort scripts for a human-decision field
Result: better
Gate: contract — prop-registry extension and a review-console subject kind; the badge copy is a claim-shape change on a reader-facing surface
evidence:
- `features/civicscore/getLeaderboardData.ts:569-577` — effort verdict props read raw, no state
- `features/profile/getProfileData.ts:538-558` — prose fields behind `publicCopyOrNull` only
- `features/civicscore/components/LowScoreReasonChip.tsx:52`, `WorkhorseBadge.tsx:66-67` — date, count, no rung
- `lib/analysis/low-score-reason.ts:27, 53-54, 90` — closed vocabulary with tone, no review dimension
- `lib/claims/claim.ts:33` — `ClaimReviewStatus = "verified" | "pending" | "rejected" | "ungated"` exists for figures, unused for verdicts
- `docs/routes/zebricek.md:159-164` — sentinel: non-contribution layers have zero invariants
- registry technique `structural-low-score-corrections` §"Stored as a separate reviewable fact"

title: Moved citations shown with both sides: as-of re-derivation from the bitemporal g
body:
## Summary
A stale `/graf/p/[ref]` says only "hash in address ≠ hash today"; the reader never sees WHAT changed. The store already keeps bitemporal history and an `asOf()` read, used by nothing outside tests and a repair script — the permalink could re-derive the cited view at its issue instant and print the diff.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T1 (As-of re-derivation: moved/gone claims shown with both sides from the bitemporal store); deck rank #13 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

`getPermalinkData` re-derives from today's store and sets `fresh: currentHash === decoded.hash` (`features/graph/getPermalinkData.ts:160-189`); the page posts `staleNotice` with two hashes (`PermalinkPage.tsx:501-507`), the card model gives `citedHash` (`permalink.ts` `permalinkCardModel`), and `/overeni` maps `fresh` → `verified | moved` with nothing but the two hashes (`features/overeni/verdict.ts:183-199`). The address `g.<state>.<hash8>` carries no issue time (`permalink.ts:148-164`), so even with history the server cannot know WHEN the citation was minted; `retrievedOn` exists only in the copy-paste citation line. Meanwhile `kg_edge_history`/`kg_node_history` record `valid_from/valid_to/recorded_at/superseded_at` (`ddl.ts:327-337`) and `KgAsOfReads` + `asOf(at)` (`lib/db/pglite/repositories/kg.ts:44-67, 388-410`) replay the graph as known at an instant; `grep -rl "asOf("` finds only the repo itself, its tests and `kg-repair-orphans.ts`. The registry's vocabulary requires `moved` to be "shown with both sides and both dates"; today the product shows one side and one date.

Built: a second address shape `g2.<state>.<hash8>.<issuedAt YYYYMMDD>` decoded beside `g.` (append-only address space; `g.` keeps working as "moved without a replay date"). `resolveView` gains an `at` parameter and every graph loader gets an `asOf`-parametrised twin over the same pure code (`buildTrails`, `buildPathAdjacency`, `getNodeDetail` take a `KgAsOfReads` instead of the live store — the memo cells stay live-only). On `fresh: false` the page renders the then-view and the now-view through one pure `diffViews()` (edges added/removed, gate flips, weight changes, node facts changed, path re-routed), with each side dated; the JSON-LD bundle carries `hasPart` for both with `validFrom`/`validThrough`; `/overeni` prints the diff table under `moved`; the OG card says "změněno od <date>".

## Flow
- `permalink.ts`: `encodeGraphRef` emits `g2.` with `issuedAt`; `decodeGraphRef` accepts both; `GraphRef.issuedAt: string | null`; tests for refusal on malformed dates (no repair).
- `db-repositories`: extend `KgAsOfReads` with `kgNeighbours` parity (already in the interface) and assert `asOf(now)` row-identity is covered by `kg-bitemporal.test.ts`; expose `store.asOf` through `lib/db/store.ts`'s public type.

Readers who arrive from a months-old article see exactly which tie was rejected, which contract appeared, which hop re-routed — the difference between "this citation is stale" and "this citation was wrong".
