title: Identity ledger — one cross-source person resolution table with confidence and a
body:
## Summary
Four adapters resolve "is this registry person our MP" with four private rules — exact birth date (ARES VR, dataor), folded full name with region/elected tie-breaks (volby), a Hlídač bridge — and the answer lives only as props on whichever edge the adapter was building. There is no table of person identities across sources, so a confirmation made for one tie is invisible to the next adapter, a rejection is not terminal, and no surface can say "this MP is the same person as this OR officer" with a review state.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T3 (One audited review door for every claim kind (bill verdicts, effort verdicts, identity, corrections, exposure)); deck rank #14 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

`scripts/case-loops/money/reconcile-ares-vr.ts:6-8` matches "by EXACT birth date … never a name-only guess"; `dataor-corroborate.ts:25-26` repeats the rule against the bulk export; `lib/ingest/sources/volby.ts:274-307` joins MPs to PS2025 candidates "by folded full name", disambiguating by region then by `elected` and returning `matched|ambiguous|unmatched`; `lib/analysis/money-feed.ts:488/516` `bridgePerson`/`bridgeSearchByBirthdate` bridge psp.cz → Hlídač. Each writes its verdict where it happens to be standing: `corroboration` on `linked_to` edges, `bridge_provenance` on person nodes (`prop-registry.json` nodes.person), a `JoinStatus` in a batch payload. `lib/ingest/sources/dataor.ts:178-184` records that officer birth dates are extracted "ONLY to compare against our own roster birth date" — the comparison itself is re-implemented per script. The kernel says the human gate flips only `review_state` on ties (`docs/case-loops.md` Authority) — identity, the claim underneath every tie, has no gate at all. "Built" is a `person_identity` table (`person_psp_id`, `source` ∈ {ares-vr, dataor, volby, hlidac, kiosek}, `source_key`, `method` ∈ {birthdate-exact, name-fold+region, bridge}, `confidence`, `review_state`, `decided_by`, `audit_id`) written through ONE repository (append-only audit like `review_audit`), one pure `lib/analysis/identity.ts` holding the match rules (imported by all four adapters, with the `czech-civic-data` fold as the only name normalizer), a `/penize/kontrola` lane "totožnost" for `ambiguous` rows, and every tie-building path (`kg-money-ingest`, `reconcile-ares-vr`, `dataor-corroborate`, the volby signal, kiosek `concerns`) resolving through the ledger first — an unconfirmed identity yields a `pending_review` tie, a rejected identity yields no tie and stays rejected on re-run.

## Flow
- Add `person_identity` + its audit to CORE_DDL (`npm run db:migrate`), a repository outside the `Store` facade (the `ledger.ts`/`changes.ts` precedent), and a `Store`-free reader for loaders.
- Extract the four matching rules into `lib/analysis/identity.ts` (pure, fixture-tested: exact-birthdate, name-fold with region/elected tie-break, ambiguity rules), importing `asciiFold` from `packages/czech-civic-data`.
- Backfill: derive rows from what the graph already asserts (`corroboration: registry-confirmed` ties → `ares-vr` identities confirmed-by-machine; volby `matched` rows; Hlídač bridges) with `review_state: pending_review` and the originating pass as provenance — never marked human-confirmed.
- Convert the four adapters/scripts to resolve through the ledger before building an edge; a rejected identity short-circuits; new candidates insert as `pending`.
- Review lane: extend `ReviewRepository` + the token-gated server action with an identity decision (append-only audit row first); the `/penize/kontrola` "rozpor role × rejstřík" lane links each tie to its identity row.
- Surface: `/poslanec/[id]` money block states the identity basis per tie ("shoda data narození v OR, potvrzeno strojově") through the gate vocabulary; `/overeni` mints an identity claim family.

## Expected impact
The reviewer who opens the first human-gate session (money STATE item 0) decides identity once per (MP, registry person) instead of once per tie, and the decision holds across every later adapter run; a namesake can never re-enter as a fresh lead after rejection; the platform can finally print, per tie, which identity method stands behind it. Measured by: rows in `person_identity` vs distinct (MP, source key) pairs currently implied by ties (211 ties → fewer identities), and the share of ties whose identity row is `pending` vs human-decided. What could break: the backfill must not upgrade any machine match to human-confirmed; the volby name join is a lead-grade method and must never seed a `linked_to` tie by itself.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality | resilience - identity becomes one claim with one rule set and one door, instead of four private rules with no memory
Before: 4 matching implementations in 4 files (`reconcile-ares-vr.ts`, `dataor-corroborate.ts`, `volby.ts:274-307`, `money-feed.ts:488-530`); 0 tables holding a person-to-source identity; identity decisions stored as edge props (`corroboration`) or batch payload fields; 211 ties all `pending_review` and the gate "never exercised" (money STATE)
After: 1 rule module, 1 table, N identity rows with a review state; every tie resolves through a row — the instrument is the ledger's `review_state` histogram and the count of adapters importing `lib/analysis/identity.ts`
Method: probe - read of the four matchers, the prop registry and the case-loop authority rules
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy
evidence:
- `scripts/case-loops/money/reconcile-ares-vr.ts:6-8` — "matches the MP against the officer/shareholder list by EXACT birth date … never a name-only guess"
- `scripts/case-loops/money/dataor-corroborate.ts:25-26` — "Exact-birthdate match against the roster (same discipline as reconcile-ares-vr.ts — NEVER a name-only guess)"
- `lib/ingest/sources/volby.ts:263` `export type JoinStatus = "matched" | "ambiguous" | "unmatched";` `:274-307` — folded-name join, region and elected-pool tie-breaks
- `lib/analysis/money-feed.ts:488` `export function bridgePerson(`; `:516` `export function bridgeSearchByBirthdate(`
- `lib/ingest/sources/dataor.ts:178-184` — birth dates extracted "ONLY to compare against our own roster birth date"
- `lib/kg/prop-registry.json` → `nodes.person` includes `bridge_provenance`; `edges.linked_to` carries corroboration state (per `memory/money-stored-review-rank-is-a-stale-cache.md`)
- `docs/data-analysis/case-money/STATE.md` — "ties · review state: 211 · all `pending_review` — the human gate has never been exercised"
- `docs/case-loops.md` Authority — "No loop, at any autonomy level, flips a `review_state` … only a human verifies"
- `docs/ROADMAP.md:59-61` — "Entity-resolution service with confidence + human-review gate is the critical component"

title: Vote figures enter the claim gate: a `vote` claim dataset for /overeni
body:
## Summary
The most-quoted numbers of this group — a named MP's rebellion rate, a club's cohesion, the reconciliation discrepancy count, the volby contested record — cannot be pasted into /overeni and re-derived, because no vote figure mints a claim ref and the live resolver knows only money, score and law.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T2 (A claim address on every figure: registry-keyed citations, figure receipts, exports and the machine gate); deck rank #15 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

`features/overeni/liveFigures.ts:66-70` enumerates `LIVE_DATASETS` as `MONEY`, `SCORE`, `LAW`; `features/lawwatch/lawClaims.ts` shows the pattern (subject codec, metric, gate state, basis = corpus aggregate, refusals for un-formable subjects). `features/votetrack/**` mints nothing: the only occurrences of „claim" are the kompas URL codec and tests; `RealRebellions.tsx`, `RealDisciplineBoard.tsx` and the seismograf print `topRebels[].rate`, `clubs[].cohesion`, `reconciliation` counts and `coverage.thresholdDiffers` (`record/derive.ts:480-496, 434-446, 507-514, 543`) as plain numbers with a `SourceNote`, never through `CitableNumber`. /volby carries the gap forward: `lib/analysis/volby/types.ts:36` lets evidence refs be `claim:…`, and `docs/routes/volby.md` records that „the baseline `source` refs (`claim:volby-census:…`) are labels, not yet resolvable at `/zdroj`". So a journalist who quotes „rebeloval v 12 % hlasování" from /poslanec has nothing to paste into the gate that would re-run the definition.

Built: `features/votetrack/voteClaims.ts` mints refs for four metrics with subject codecs that already exist — `psp:person:<pspId>` (rebellion rate + eligible population, floor `MIN_ELIGIBLE_VOTES` in the basis), club organ id (cohesion + `riceVotes`, floor `MIN_CLUB_POSITIONAL`), the chamber (reconciliation discrepancies over `valid`, threshold-differs over `valid`), and a vote id (contestedness, `MIN_POSITIONAL_BALLOTS` from `contested.ts:57`). Gate state is `ungated` (deterministic arithmetic, the lawClaims precedent for census claims); basis is `coverage.from…to` + `valid` + the imported floor. `liveFigures.ts` adds `VOTE_CLAIM_DATASET` and re-derives through `getFullVoteRecord()` — a cold miss costs the ~16 s ledger read the memo already amortises, an unreadable ledger answers `unavailable`, a person below the floor answers with the floor, not `gone`. The kompas alignment is explicitly REFUSED as a claim: it is the reader's artefact (the compass subject's lens rule), and the refusal is written in the module beside the mint.

## Flow
- `voteClaims.ts` + tests: subject codecs, metric enum, basis, refusals (below-floor, unaffiliated, voided vote, kompas alignment).
- `CitableNumber` on the rebel board, club board, reconciliation sentence, threshold coverage, /poslanec rebellion header, /volby contested rows (`FindingRow.tsx` already renders refs).
- `liveFigures.ts`: dataset + resolver branch; `liveFiguresRoundTrip.test.ts` extended with a vote fixture.
- /volby baseline refs become resolvable or are renamed as labels (no half-state).
- `docs/routes/{hlasovani,overeni,volby}.md` entries; `require-source-citation` count stays flat.

## Expected impact
Newsrooms can verify a rebellion or cohesion figure against today's record with the definition attached; the volby ledger stops carrying refs that resolve nowhere. Measured by the count of rendered vote figures wrapped in `CitableNumber` and by round-trip tests. What could break: a re-derivation on a cold ledger takes seconds — the verdict surface must stream or state the wait, never time out into `gone`.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every published vote figure is re-derivable at the gate with its floor and population
Before: `LIVE_DATASETS` = 3 datasets, 0 vote metrics; 0 `CitableNumber` in `features/votetrack`; volby `claim:volby-census:…` refs unresolvable
After: N vote figures citable (rebel rate ×12 rows, cohesion × clubs, 2 chamber counts, contested × rows) and 4 metrics resolvable at /overeni; instrument = grep of `CitableNumber` under `features/votetrack` + the round-trip test
Method: probe - grep for claims/CitableNumber across the group and read the resolver's dataset set
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence:
- `features/overeni/liveFigures.ts:66-70` — `LIVE_DATASETS = {MONEY, SCORE, LAW}`
- `features/lawwatch/lawClaims.ts` — the mint pattern; `lib/analysis/volby/types.ts:36` — `ref = h.<edge> | u.<node> | claim:…`
- `features/votetrack/record/derive.ts:479-496` (`topRebels`, `qualifiedRebels`), `:434-446` (`clubs[].cohesion`, `riceVotes`), `:507-514` (reconciliation), `:543` (threshold summary)
- `lib/analysis/volby/contested.ts:57` — `MIN_POSITIONAL_BALLOTS = 100`
- grep `CitableNumber|claimRef` over `features/votetrack` → only `kompas/codec.ts`, tests

title: Every export carries a verifiable address: poster, embed and OG go through the g
body:
## Summary
The three artifacts most likely to leave the site — the printed poster (`PosterFrame`), the iframe embed (`app/embed/zebricek`) and the OG images — carry a source line and a live URL but no claim address; pasting what they print into `/overeni` answers `politicas-neni-citace`, so the least-correctable outputs are exactly the ones the gate cannot verify.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T2 (A claim address on every figure: registry-keyed citations, figure receipts, exports and the machine gate); deck rank #16 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

`buildPosterCitation` (`features/shared/poster/citation.ts`) composes source · as-of · methodology · pass · formula-mismatch · `liveLine` = `posterDisplayUrl(sourceUrl)` — a SURFACE URL (`/zebricek`), and `PosterFrame.tsx:94-110` prints it. The embed footer (`features/landing/referendum/embed.ts:102`) prints "zdroj: politicas — otevřený index přispění · psp.cz, deterministický výpočet · ‹status›" with an `href` to the leaderboard. `refDetect.ts:129-132` recognises only `/zdroj/`, `/graf/p/`, `/dashboard/exponat/` paths and `claim:` refs; a surface path is answered with `politicas-neni-citace` (`docs/routes/overeni.md`). Only `/graf/p/[ref]` has a fingerprinted OG image (`app/graf/p/[ref]/opengraph-image.tsx:90-126` reads `pending`/`fresh`); `app/opengraph-image.tsx` and `app/referendum/og/route.tsx` carry none. So the artifacts that get screenshotted into articles are addressable only to a page whose content moves daily — "the footnote that outlives its number".

"Built" = ONE export-address builder in `features/shared/provenance/` (`exportRef.ts`): for a poster/embed/OG it issues an address that carries what was claimed — the metric family's `claim:` ref(s) or the view fingerprint + the as-of day + the derivation (`CONTRIBUTION_FORMULA_REF`/pass) — and `refDetect` learns the family so pasting the printed line yields the 3-verdict answer with "moved" showing both dates (ties into card 3). `PosterCitation` gains `claimLine` (typeset by `PosterFrame` as a 4th footer line, and as a QR rendered from the same string — QR is a typographic form of the address, not a second address); the embed footer's `href` becomes the export address and the `<div class="foot">` carries `data-claim-*` from `lib/format.ts formatCitable` so a scraped embed still testifies; every OG route posts the as-of and the pending count the way `/graf/p`'s does, through one shared `ogCitationLines()`. The poster's existing honesty (`posterUndatedNote`, `posterProvenanceNote` for mixed/absent provenance) carries into the address: an undated or mixed sheet issues an address WITHOUT a date/derivation segment, and the gate then says so — it never fabricates the day.

## Flow
- `exportRef.ts`: pure encode/decode (append-only grammar, refuse-not-repair, `MAX_REF_LENGTH` discipline from `claimRef.ts`), unit-tested for byte-stable serialisation.
- `refDetect` gains the `export` family; `verdict.ts` maps it onto the figura/graf verdicts it already has (no fourth verdict).
- `citation.ts` + `PosterFrame`: `claimLine` + QR (SVG path, tokens only, no external lib per DESIGN §1).
- `embed.ts`: footer `href` = export address; `data-claim-*` attributes on the figure cells via `formatCitable`.
- `app/opengraph-image.tsx`, `app/referendum/og/route.tsx`: shared `ogCitationLines()` printing as-of + pending count + short address.
- `docs/routes/{overeni,landing,zebricek}.md` records; `liveFiguresRoundTrip.test.ts` extended with an export address per metric.

## Expected impact
A printed sheet on a notice board or an embedded widget in a news article can be pasted into `/overeni` and answered; corrections become findable from the artifact itself (right of reply needs the address on the thing the subject saw). Measured: export lanes with a gate-recognised address (1 of 5 today: graf OG only → 5). What could break: the poster footer is a print artifact — the extra line must fit A4 within the `poster-sheet` print layer (`globals.css`) or the sheet overflows.

## Evaluation
Claim: user — every artifact that leaves the site can be re-verified at /overeni
Before: poster `liveLine` = surface URL; embed footer `href` = leaderboard; `refDetect` path families = 3; pasting a poster's URL → `politicas-neni-citace`; 1 of 3 OG routes fingerprinted
After: all export lanes issue a decodable address; the round-trip test enumerates them
Method: probe — read `citation.ts`, `PosterFrame.tsx` footer, `embed.ts:102`, `refDetect.ts:129-132`, the three OG routes
Result: better
Gate: contract — a new address family in the append-only ref grammar
evidence: - `features/shared/poster/citation.ts` `liveLine: \`živá verze: ${displayUrl}\`` and `posterDisplayUrl(input.sourceUrl)`; `PosterFrame.tsx:99,106` retrieved/live lines only - `features/landing/referendum/embed.ts:102` `zdroj: politicas — otevřený index přispění · psp.cz, deterministický výpočet` - `features/overeni/refDetect.ts:129-132` `PATH_PATTERNS` = zdroj, graf, exponat; `docs/routes/overeni.md` "`politicas-neni-citace` … our page but not a citable address" - OG routes: `app/opengraph-image.tsx`, `app/referendum/og/route.tsx` (no fingerprint), `app/graf/p/[ref]/opengraph-image.tsx:90-126` (pending + fresh) - `lib/format.ts:160-166` `formatCitable` returns `data-claim-*` attrs — reusable in the embed's static HTML - registry golden path: "those claims leave the platform immediately … copied into articles, screenshots, and arguments"

title: Declared attribution perimeter + a downward exposure lane in the review console
body:
## Summary
The perimeter of "firms tied to this MP" is the MP's own Hlídač-listed roles, one hop, and it is declared nowhere on the surface; the graph now holds 113 dated `owns_stake` edges (84 current) that the product reads only upward for classification, never downward from an owner-operator's firm to the subsidiaries that actually sign the contracts.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 5 scout(s), theme T3 (One audited review door for every claim kind (bill verdicts, effort verdicts, identity, corrections, exposure)); deck rank #17 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

`kg-money.ts:39-45` states the tie source (declarations / OR officer records) and `money-feed.ts` builds every tie from a person's own `udalosti[]`; `ownership.ts:15-19` rule 1: "ONE hop … no chain walk, no exposure"; `ownership-depth2.ts` (batches 016-018) walks UPWARD to find public owners. `TrailMethod.tsx` prints four steps and no perimeter (`features/money/components/TrailMethod.tsx:2`; `grep perimet` → 0 hits in `features/money`). The registry says a direct-ties-only table is a floor of the reachable surface and the copy must say so; and that the downward walk is the legitimate way to grow the candidate set without asserting exposure. On the live store the case exists: AGROFERT a.s. carries the attributable tie (Babiš `manager`, 8,71 mil. Kč — `docs/routes/penize.md`), while the group's operating firms (Lovochemie, PRECHEZA, Fatra, Kostelecké uzeniny — b019's contradiction list) sit in the graph as steward-class dozorčí-rada ties or as `owns_stake` counterparts, their contract volume outside every attributable figure and outside every review lane.

Built: (1) `ATTRIBUTION_PERIMETER` as a versioned constant in `reachableMoney.ts` (`{ subjects: "official-only", relations: ["registered-role","direct-holding"], depth: 1, stakeThreshold: null, version: "perimeter-v1" }`) rendered verbatim in `TrailMethod`, the metodika, the packet `citeCs` and the claim derivation string (`moneyDerivation`), so every reach figure names its inclusion rule and the "nejméně" wording gains its second reason. (2) A pure `exposureBreadth(tie, ownsStakeOut)` in a new `features/money/exposure.ts`: for each attributable tie's company, one hop DOWN over current `owns_stake` edges to subsidiaries, collecting each subsidiary's `CompanyContracts` via the existing `readCompanySupplies` — output is structure (rows: subsidiary, stake wording, period, contracts count/czk, `moneyReachesCompany`-filtered), never added to any bucket. (3) A seventh console lane „expozice přes vlastnictví" listing those rows with a reviewer action that can only create a NEW `linked_to` lead (`pending_review`, source = the chain, provenance = the two edges) — never a class change, never a figure; (4) on `/penize/firma/[ico]` the ownership block gains "dceřiné firmy v grafu: n, smluv m" as counts with links, no CZK on the parent's file. Depth and fetch budget ship with the result (`walked / not attempted` counts), per the technique.

## Flow
- Declare `ATTRIBUTION_PERIMETER` (one definition), thread into `TrailMethod`, `/metodika` money section, `packet.ts` cite block, `moneyClaims.moneyDerivation`; messages pin the sentence shape.
- `exposure.ts` pure module + tests over `owns_stake` fixtures (open vs closed period, sole-owner wording, non-canonical counterpart → dropped and counted).
- Loader: extend `loadCompanyMoneySlice` (already reads `owns_stake` both legs, `moneyLoader.ts:820-862`) to fetch subsidiaries' supplies via `companySuppliesMemo`; cap + `truncated` threaded.
- Console: new lane driven by the same predicate; action `proposeLeadFromChain` in `reviewActions.ts` writes a `linked_to` edge `pending_review` with `source: "ownership-chain:<parent>→<child>"` and appends an audit row; the human gate then decides it like any tie.
- Company file: subsidiaries block (counts + links); parent file never gains money.
- Symmetry check script: run the walk over ALL attributable ties, report per-club counts of chain leads before the lane ships (whole population or nothing).

## Expected impact
Readers see what "firms tied to" means and why the figure is a floor; reviewers get the one lead class the current perimeter structurally hides (holding → operating firm) as leads with the chain attached; no headline moves until a human verifies a chain-born tie. Measured: chain leads found (n ties, m subsidiaries, contract volume outside all buckets today), per-club distribution, and after the first gate session how many became `verified`/`rejected`. Could break: nothing numeric; the risk is copy — a lane that reads as an accusation, hence the lead-only action and the counts-not-CZK rule on the parent file.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the inclusion rule becomes a published, versioned part of the metric and the review queue sees the evasive tie class
Before: 0 perimeter statements on any money surface; 0 downward chain reads (`ownership.ts` rule 1); 113 `owns_stake` edges used only for the company axis
After: perimeter printed with every reach figure; MISSING INSTRUMENT: the count of subsidiaries reachable one hop down from the 18 owner-operator MPs' firms and their contract volume — computable today on a store copy, not yet computed
Method: probe - grep for perimeter copy, read ownership.ts rules, batch 016-018 walk direction, b019 contradiction list
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy
evidence:
- `lib/analysis/kg-money.ts:39-45`; `lib/analysis/money-feed.ts:1-30` — tie perimeter = the person's own declared roles.
- `features/money/ownership.ts:15-19` — "JEN ZAPSANÉ VLASTNICTVÍ, JEDEN KROK … žádná expozice".
- `features/money/components/TrailMethod.tsx:2` — four steps, no perimeter; no `perimet*` token under `features/money`.
- `features/money/moneyLoader.ts:820-862` — `owns_stake` already read both directions per company.
- `docs/data-analysis/case-money/STATE.md` — 113 `owns_stake` edges / 84 current; 18 role×register contradictions (AGROFERT-group dozorčí rady).
- `features/money/reachableMoney.ts:137-140` — attribution rule has role and company axes, no perimeter axis.

title: Buyer edge for Registr smluv contracts — the authority as a graph endpoint
body:
## Summary
Every harvested contract knows who published it (`publisher: {ico, nazev}` on the contract node), but the publishing authority is a string prop, not a node — so the graph can answer "which companies tied to MPs supply the state" and cannot answer "which MP-tied companies does THIS obec pay", while `/volby` builds its zadavatel pages from the ISVZ tender layer alone.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 4 scout(s), theme T7 (The municipality as one graph subject across /rozpocty, /volby, /penize and the deník); deck rank #18 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

`scripts/case-loops/money/persist-contract-harvest.ts:141` writes `publisher: rec.subjekt ? { ico: rec.subjekt.ico, nazev: rec.subjekt.nazev } : null` onto the contract node; `supplies` edges run company → contract only (`prop-registry.json` → `edges.supplies` carries `direction`, `recipients_shared`). The tender loop already mints authority nodes as ordinary `company:ico:*` and links them with `procures` (`scripts/case-loops/tender/persist-month.ts:146-148`), and `/volby` reads exactly that fold — "kind `tender` nodes + `procures`/`wins` edges + authority `company` nodes" (`docs/routes/volby.md:30-33`) — so an obec's page shows its tenders but none of its signed contracts, even where the harvest holds them. `smlouvy-dump.ts:32-42` (the `party_idnum` vs `subject_idnum` finding) and `harvest-contract-dumps.ts:41-45` (`publisherOnlyByIco` — publisher-side matches dropped, "kept as an auditable total") show the group has measured the buyer side and deliberately parked it. "Built" is an `awards` edge authority → contract (register fact: the `<subjekt>` of the record; weight = the contract's `amount` with its `amountBasis`; props `{platce, prijemce}` verbatim), authority nodes minted through the SAME `mintCompany` rule the tender loop uses (CZE only, 8-padded IČO, `memory/ico-node-id-canonical-form.md`), a `publisherOnly` harvest mode that keeps the records the current allow-list drops (the steward institutions' own contracting, sized in the state file), and a shared `features/volby/tenderLayer.ts`-style contract fold so `/volby/obec/[ico]` and `/volby/kraj/[slug]` render "smlouvy s firmami napojenými na poslance" beside tenders. `moneyReachesCompany()` / `tieIsAttributable()` stay the only attribution rules — the buyer edge adds an endpoint, never a new claim of reach.

## Flow
- Amend `KG_EDGE_RELS` with `awards`; register `awards` props (`amount`, `amountBasis`, `platce`, `prijemce`, `direction_basis`) in `prop-registry.json` + `graph-schema.md`.
- Extract `mintCompany`/`isCzech` from `tender/persist-month.ts` into `lib/analysis/company-node.ts` (one definition) and import it from both persisters.
- `persist-contract-harvest.ts`: emit `awards` edges from `rec.subjekt` for every harvested record (existing and new), merge-preserving; disclose records whose `subjekt.ico` is null or foreign as a counted gap.
- `harvest-contract-dumps.ts --publisher-side`: for the arena authorities `/volby` serves (obce/kraje IČOs from `mirrorData.ts`), keep records where `subjekt.ico` is in the allow-list, bounded and disclosed (`every cap ships its population`), never a bulk personal-data corpus.
- Fold + surface: an `awards` read in the volby loader with `warnIfTruncated`, a `SourceNote` per figure citing `sourceUrl`; `/penize/firma/[ico]` gains "kdo platí" (payers by authority) using the same fold.
- Re-run `reachable-metric-audit.ts` and `supplies-coverage-audit.ts` on a copy to prove `/penize`'s headline is unchanged (the buyer edge must not move attribution).

## Expected impact
A voter on `/volby/obec/[ico]` sees the register's own record of what their town signed with MP-tied companies — the first Registr smluv fact on the flagship voter surface; the money case files can name the paying authority; the tender loop's "authority" and the contract corpus's "publisher" become one node with one IČO rule. Measured by: `awards` edges ≈ harvested contract count (currently 2 287 + the batch-012 harvest), and the number of obec/kraj pages with ≥1 `awards` row. What could break: `awards` on a `payer` record would read as money flowing to the supplier — carry `platce/prijemce` verbatim and never let `awards` feed `moneyReachesCompany`.

## Evaluation
Claim: user | quality - both endpoints of a public payment resolved through registry identifiers
Before: 0 authority → contract edges (edge rels: `supplies`, `procures`, `bids_on`, `wins` only); `publisher` exists only as a jsonb prop on contract nodes; `/volby` zadavatel pages read the tender fold only
After: `awards` edge count vs harvested contracts (disclosed split: CZE IČO / foreign / missing); obec pages with ≥1 register contract — the instrument is the volby loader's `awards` count per arena
Method: probe - read of the persister, the tender persister, the prop registry and the volby route contract
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
evidence:
- `scripts/case-loops/money/persist-contract-harvest.ts:141` `publisher: rec.subjekt ? { ico: rec.subjekt.ico, nazev: rec.subjekt.nazev } : null,`
- `lib/kg/prop-registry.json` → `edges` = `[amends, assigned_to, owns_stake, supplies, cites, belongs_to, owns, co_votes_with, influential_in, linked_to, proposes_amendment, rebels_against, spoke_on, sponsors, rapporteur, procures, bids_on, wins]` — no authority → contract relation
- `scripts/case-loops/tender/persist-month.ts:146-148` — `mintCompany(l.authority)` + `rel: "procures"` from `company:ico:${l.authority.ico}`
- `docs/routes/volby.md:30-33` — reads "kind `tender` nodes + `procures`/`wins` edges + authority `company` nodes"
- `lib/ingest/sources/smlouvy-dump.ts:106-111` — `platce`/`prijemce` direction flags; `:32-42` in `smlouvy.ts` — `party_idnum` misses publisher-side contracts
- `scripts/case-loops/money/harvest-contract-dumps.ts:41-45` — `publisherOnlyByIco` dropped-but-counted
- `memory/supplies-is-not-attribution.md`, `memory/attribution-has-two-axes.md` — reach stays with `moneyReachesCompany` / `tieIsAttributable`

## Expected impact

title: The municipality as a graph subject shared by /rozpocty, /volby and /penize
body:
## Summary
The obec exists three times: as a packed registry row + a frozen pass-41 supplier batch on `/rozpocty`, as an authority `company` node with `electoral_arena` in the tender layer on `/volby`, and as an owner node in `owns_stake` on `/penize/firma`. There is no municipality node kind, so the three surfaces cannot cite one address, the trail is 33 passes stale, and the budget covers 132 of 6 254 obce although the bulk source covers all.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 4 scout(s), theme T7 (The municipality as one graph subject across /rozpocty, /volby, /penize and the deník); deck rank #20 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

- `/rozpocty`'s supplier trail is a checked-in batch: `SUPPLIERS_PASS = 41`, `SUPPLIERS_RETRIEVED_ON = "2026-07-27"` (`features/budget/data/municipalSuppliers.generated.ts:10-13`); the graph is at pass 74 (`docs/data-analysis/case-tender/STATE.md`) with batch-014's `direction` semantics and batch-015/018's `public_mandate` — none of which the trail sees. `deriveMunicipalSupplierRows` re-derives direction from `partyDirections` with its own two-party rule (`features/budget/supplierTrail.ts:243-256`) rather than importing `moneyReachesCompany`; `getSupplierTies` joins ties live but against the stale IČO set (`features/budget/getSupplierTies.ts:36-43`).
- Budget series: `SNAPSHOT_FLOOR_POPULATION = 10000`, 132 towns (`budgetSnapshots.generated.ts:13`), while `docs/data-analysis/budget-sources.md` verifies the FINM bulk ZIP carries every obec per period and the SIMU API gives debt p.c. + population per IČO. `peerGroups.ts:9-11, 30` then widens to the whole country at `MIN_PEERS = 5` because the kraj group is thin — a small-sample widening forced by the ingest cap, not by the population.
- `/volby` folds obce as authority `company` nodes and corrects `electoral_arena` from the 6 254-obec registry at read time (`features/volby/tenderLayer.ts:19-29`), and it explicitly refuses "any obec↔authority link beyond IČO equality (příspěvkovky and city companies are the national `nejasne` count, never localised)" (`docs/routes/volby.md`); the tender STATE's open item 1 is exactly that: resolve 1 575 `nejasne` authorities via ownership/legal form with `public-body.ts`.
- `graph-schema.md:37-45` has no municipality kind; `public-body.ts` already knows form 801/811/804 (`lib/analysis/public-body.ts:52-57`), and `owns_stake` already carries Město Plzeň / Praha as parents (`features/money/ownership.ts:5-9`).

Built: a `municipality:<ico>` node kind (or a declared `company` subtype keyed by legal form 801/811/804 — one ruling, recorded) carrying the registry props (name, kraj, population per period) and yearly FINM/SIMU budget props for ALL obce; edges: `party_to` municipality→contract with the register's own direction flag (the money graph already holds `parties`/`partyDirections` on contract nodes — `supplierTrail.ts:225-243`), `procures` (exists), `founded`/`owns_stake` municipality→příspěvková organizace / city company from ARES VR (the `ownership-from-vr.ts` tool, generalised). Then: `/rozpocty`'s trail becomes an indexed `kgNeighbours` read on the municipality node (the `/penize/firma` pattern: `loadCompanyMoneySlice`), the batch file is deleted; the "doložená platba" rule and the reach rule are one import; `/volby`'s arena correction reads the node instead of the packed registry; the `nejasne` class resolves through the disclosed one-hop ownership edge and stays SEPARATE from the town's own figure (clause 1: never summed upward — rendered as "zřizuje / vlastní", a link, not a number); the budget mirror's peer groups widen only when the population is genuinely thin.

## Flow
- Ruling first: node kind vs subtype; record in `graph-schema.md` + prop-registry; municipality id = canonical 8-digit IČO (`companyId.ts`).
- Ingest: FINM bulk + SIMU per IČO for all obce (annual, cached) → `municipality` props by period; registry props from the existing generator; pass-stamped via `persist-batch.ts`.
- Edges: `party_to` from contract node `parties`/`publisher` (already in the graph, no network); `founded`/`owns_stake` from ARES VR (`spolecnici`/`zakladatel`) for obce ≥ the tender authority set first, all obce later; every edge dated + sourced.
- Reads: `features/budget/getTownData.ts` server loader (`kgNeighbours` on the municipality node for `party_to` + `procures`, then per-company `readCompanySupplies`); `supplierTrail.ts` keeps its pure derivation but consumes graph rows and imports `moneyReachesCompany`; `generate-municipal-suppliers.ts` retired.
- `/volby`: `tenderLayer.ts` arena from the node; `nejasne` resolution via the one-hop edge; the `/volby/obec/[ico]` page and `/rozpocty/[ico]` link each other and cite the same claim subject (`municipality:<ico>`).
- Claims: `MONEY_METRIC` gains `smlouvy-obce`; `/zdroj` re-derives from the node read.
- Peer groups: recompute `MIN_PEERS` widening over the full population; print the sample per median (already the rule).

## Expected impact
A voter looking up their town gets one address that carries budget, contracts (live, direction-disclosed), tender radar and the town's own companies as a disclosed hop — instead of a 2026-07-27 snapshot beside a pass-74 radar. Measured: trail staleness (days since `SUPPLIERS_RETRIEVED_ON` → same-pass as the graph), budget coverage 132 → 6 254 obce, `nejasne` authorities resolved with a cited owner (0 → n of 1 575), peer-group scope "celostátní" share before/after. Could break: `/rozpocty` becomes a store-dependent route (needs the honest `DataUnavailable` path the doc already mandates) and ~360 prerendered town pages become dynamic like every other route (`revalidate-is-inert` memory).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one municipality subject, live and cited, replaces three unlinked representations
Before: trail batch pass 41 vs graph pass 74; budget 132/6 254 obce; 1 575 `nejasne` authorities unresolved; 0 municipality nodes
After: same-pass trail; budget on every obec; MISSING INSTRUMENT: a per-obec coverage tile (budget years / contracts / tenders / owned bodies) that does not exist because no node holds the obec
Method: probe - compared the generated constants with STATE.md passes; read the trail's private direction rule and volby's registry correction
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
evidence:
- `features/budget/data/municipalSuppliers.generated.ts:10-22`; `features/budget/data/budgetSnapshots.generated.ts:13-16`.
- `features/budget/supplierTrail.ts:9-24, 193-199, 243-256` — published rule, weight-only read, private direction test.
- `features/budget/getSupplierTies.ts:36-58` — live ties keyed on the batch's IČO set.
- `features/budget/peerGroups.ts:9-11, 30` — widening at `MIN_PEERS = 5`.
- `features/volby/tenderLayer.ts:19-29`; `docs/routes/volby.md` "What it refuses to derive".
- `docs/data-analysis/case-tender/STATE.md` open item 1 (1 575 `nejasne`, 134,8 mld. floor).
- `docs/data-analysis/budget-sources.md` — FINM bulk for all obce verified live.
- `docs/data-analysis/graph-schema.md:37-45` — no municipality kind; `lib/analysis/public-body.ts:52-57` — forms 801/804/811.

title: Release-stamped entity sitemap — case files discoverable without per-request sca
body:
## Summary
The sitemap deliberately omits every entity case file — `/poslanec/[id]`, `/zakony/[cislo]`, `/penize/firma/[ico]`, `/zdroj/[ref]` — because listing them "would mean enumerating specific MPs, tisky and firms, i.e. reading the store at request time" (`publicRoutes.ts:338-343`, `sitemap.ts:449-453`); the platform's most-cited pages depend on a crawler clicking through a directory page. The release train already produces the artefact that lifts the objection: a versioned, sealed cut of the graph.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 4 scout(s), theme T7 (The municipality as one graph subject across /rozpocty, /volby, /penize and the deník); deck rank #21 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

`app/sitemap.ts:477-494` is `force-dynamic`, builds only `publicStaticRoutes(DISALLOWED_PATHS)` plus the one static registry exception (`municipalRouteIcos()`, `:455-462` — allowed precisely because it is "a static module built into the build, reads no store"), and omits `lastModified` on principle (`:469-471`: "datum poslední změny stránky nikde neevidujeme … čas sestavení odpovědi není datum změny obsahu"). `robots.ts:432` already publishes the `Sitemap:` line. `features/data-releases/manifest.ts:46-51` gives every release a `version` (`YYYY.MM.DD`) and `cutAt`; the graph-writer step that cuts a release knows exactly which entity ids exist (kind counts are already in the manifest via `kgKindCounts`).

The objection has two halves and the release train answers both: the enumeration is symmetric (every current mandate holder, every company node with a canonical IČO, every law with a dossier — never a shortlist), and the read is per RELEASE, not per request. "Built": a `release_index` (ids per kind per release version) written once by the release-cutting writer; `app/sitemap.ts` becomes a sitemap INDEX pointing at `/sitemap/<version>/poslanci.xml`, `/sitemap/<version>/firmy.xml`, `/sitemap/<version>/zakony.xml` (plus the existing static list), each generated from `release_index` (one indexed read, capped and disclosed in a comment element) with `lastModified = cutAt` — which IS a content-change date, the exact thing the current file says it lacks. `/zdroj/[ref]` stays out: receipts are minted per claim, not per entity, and a sitemap of receipts would be a fabricated enumeration.

## Flow
- `release_index` table (additive DDL via `db:migrate`; writer = the release-cut path in `scripts/data-analysis`; columns `version, kind, id`); `getDataReleasesData` exposes `entityIndexCounts` on `/data` so the sitemap's population is a published number.
- `features/shell/publicRoutes.ts`: keep `publicStaticRoutes`; add `entitySitemapRoutes(version)` returning the three sub-sitemap paths, unit-tested against `DISALLOWED_PATHS` and dynamic-route exclusion exactly as today.
- `app/sitemap.ts` → sitemap index (Next `generateSitemaps` or a manual index route); `app/sitemap/[version]/[kind]/route.ts` renders one kind from `release_index`; base URL from headers as now; an unknown version answers 404, a version whose index is empty renders an empty urlset with the population stated.
- Symmetry guard: a colocated test asserts the MP sub-sitemap's count equals the chamber's current-mandate count from the same release (the `membership` on organ 174 rule from memory) — a partial list fails the build.
- `docs/routes/app-shell.md` + `data.md`: the "přiznaná neúplnost" sentence is retired and replaced by the release-stamped rule.

## Expected impact
Search engines and archive crawlers index the 207 spisy, the firm case files and the law dossiers from a dated, complete list instead of by luck; `lastModified` becomes an honest signal. Measured by: URLs in the sitemap set 46 static + 132 obce → +207 +196 +101 (release-bound); crawl discovery of `/poslanec/*` in server logs before/after. What could break: a release cut from a degraded manifest (`degraded: true`) must not become the "latest" sitemap — reuse the manifest's own `degraded` verdict as the gate.

## Evaluation
Claim: other (reach) — the accountability record's primary pages enter the crawler's invitation list, symmetrically and dated
Before: `publicStaticRoutes()` + `municipalRouteIcos()` only; 0 entity case files in the sitemap; `lastModified` absent everywhere (`sitemap.ts:469-471`)
After: three release-stamped sub-sitemaps, counts published on `/data`; instrument: the symmetry test (sitemap MP count == current mandate holders) and the `/data` counts
Method: probe — read `sitemap.ts`, `publicRoutes.ts`, `robots.ts`, the release manifest
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract — a new table written by the release path; the sitemap index format is a public promise
evidence:
- `features/shell/publicRoutes.ts:338-343` "Dynamické segmenty … vypsat je by znamenalo vyjmenovat konkrétní poslance, tisky a firmy — tedy číst za běhu úložiště. Tahle sitemapa to VĚDOMĚ nedělá"
- `app/sitemap.ts:455-462` the municipal exception: static registry, no store read, `generateStaticParams` already emits them
- `app/sitemap.ts:469-471` `lastModified` omitted: "čas sestavení odpovědi není datum změny obsahu"
- `app/sitemap.ts:477` `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";`; `:487-490` route list = static + `municipalRouteIcos()`
- `app/robots.ts:432` `sitemap: \`${proto}://${host}/sitemap.xml\``
- `features/data-releases/manifest.ts:46-51` `version: string | null` (`YYYY.MM.DD`), `cutAt`, `degraded`
- `CLAUDE.md` route table: 207 MPs (`/zebricek`), 141 bills → 101 laws (`/zakony`), 196 companies (`money-loop` skill description)

title: Structured graph provenance: source + run + pass on every kg row, sealed per pas
body:
## Summary
`kg_node`/`kg_edge` carry a free-form `provenance jsonb` and no `source`/`ingest_run_id`, so the atlas cannot score 9 of 12 declared sources (including the entire `/penize` foundation), the Merkle seal covers eight entity tables and none of the graph, and the snapshot cannot say where a row came from.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 3 scout(s), theme T4 (Structured, sealed provenance per graph pass with a certified release); deck rank #22 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

Today: `lib/db/pglite/ddl.ts:224-246` — `kg_node(id, kind, label, props, first_seen_pass, provenance jsonb)`, `kg_edge(src, rel, dst, weight, props, provenance jsonb)`; no `source`, no `ingest_run_id`, no index on provenance. `/atlas` records the refusal verbatim (`docs/routes/atlas.md` "Unrated is structurally never zero"): "`kg_node`/`kg_edge` have no `source` column and no `ingest_run_id`, so no join key runs to `ingest_run`" — nine of the twelve `INGESTED_SOURCES` (`lib/analysis/atlas.ts:192-208`, landing `graph`) print no number, and the route file explicitly says scoring `kg_*` was ruled out because it would break the integrity rule's printed claim that "the sealed tables and the scored tables are the same set". The seal is `RUN_TABLES` (`lib/db/pglite/repositories/ledger.ts:28-37`, eight entity tables); the sentinel's `SENTINEL_ENTITY_TABLES` (`facts.ts:101-110`) is the same list, so freshness/coverage/uniformity are judged for psp entity rows only while `supplies` (19 266 in the snapshot cut), `linked_to`, `amends` and `owns_stake` — the edges readers actually cite — have no run, no seal and no freshness. The graph writers merge-preserve props (memory: `kg-upsert-replaces-props`), `persist-batch` refuses keys not in `lib/kg/prop-registry.json`, and `contribution_provenance.{pass, ref}` is the one structured stamp — precisely the one the sentinel can compare (`invariants.ts:372-417`); every other layer's stamp is whatever its writer put in `provenance`. `/data`'s snapshot ships `nodeKinds`/`edgeRels` in-cut vs in-store but cannot ship "rows per source" because the column does not exist.

Built: a provenance CONTRACT — `provenance` becomes a validated shape `{source, ingest_run_id, pass, ref, writer}` enforced by the writers (`kg-compute`, `kg-promote`, `persist-batch`, `kg-forensics`, `kg-money-ingest`) with `source` ∈ `INGESTED_SOURCES` and `ref` a declared formula/batch ref; two generated columns (`source text generated always as (provenance->>'source') stored`, `ingest_run_id bigint …`) indexed, so `ingest_run` finally joins to the graph without a rewrite of `props`; graph passes become `ingest_run` rows (they already have start/finish/status semantics) and get Merkle-sealed over the rows they wrote, extending `RUN_TABLES` by `kg_node`/`kg_edge` filtered by run. Then: `/atlas` scores all twelve sources with the same four rules and the integrity rule's printed sentence stays true; the sentinel gains `graph-provenance-uniformity` per layer (contribution, money, law) and `graph-seal` (every graph run sealed and verifying); `/data` snapshot `limits` carries in-cut vs in-store per SOURCE; `/graf/p/[ref]` and `/zdroj` receipts print the run + pass their edge came from instead of the platform's four blanket sources (the "honest carry-over" in `docs/routes/graf-permalink.md`); the historical rows whose provenance cannot be reconstructed are stamped `source: unknown` and COUNTED on `/atlas` as such — never backfilled with a plausible source.

## Flow
- `lib/kg/provenance.ts`: the one `KgProvenance` type + `assertProvenance()`; `prop-registry.json` gains the `provenance` keys; `persist-batch`/`kg-promote`/`kg-compute` refuse a write without it (behind `--allow-unstamped` for the migration pass only)
- `db:migrate`: two stored generated columns + indexes on `kg_node`/`kg_edge` (additive; `open()`'s DDL drift check must report it, snapshot first)
- Migration pass: walk every row, derive `{source, pass, ref}` from what `provenance` already holds where unambiguous (the contribution and forensic stamps are), else `source: "unknown"`; report counts per outcome; this is a `kg-promote`-style merge, never a props replace
- `ingest_run` rows for graph passes (writer = script name, note = batch id); `LedgerRepository.sealRun` extended to `kg_node`/`kg_edge where ingest_run_id = $1`; `getLedgerHeads` shows graph seals; `/data` §integrity lists them
- `/atlas`: `readEntityCoverage` over the twelve sources via the new columns; unscored list shrinks to `generated-module`/`none` landings only; `ATLAS_RULES` prose updated in the same change (rule text and score cannot drift — `messages.test.ts`)
- Sentinel: `graph-provenance-uniformity` (per layer: one `{pass, ref}` or a named split with counts), `graph-seal`, and `freshness` extended to graph sources with declared cadences
- Receipts and permalinks read `provenance.source`/`ingest_run_id` for the citation line; `sourceLinks.ts` keeps the URL rules

## Expected impact
Readers of `/atlas` see the money and law foundations scored instead of absent; a citing reader of a `supplies` edge gets its run and pass; a half-applied money pass trips the sentinel the way a half-applied score pass does. Measured by: sources scored (3 → up to 12), sealed row population (8 tables → 8 + graph runs), rows with `source: unknown` after migration (a number to burn down, printed). What could break: the writers — every kg writer touches this; and a migration that guesses a source would violate disclose-never-repair, hence `unknown` is a first-class value.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality — provenance becomes comparable over the whole graph population, not one layer
Before: 0 join keys from `kg_*` to `ingest_run`; 3/12 sources scored; 1 structured stamp (`contribution_provenance`); graph rows sealed: 0
After: 12/12 scorable; per-layer uniformity checks; every graph pass sealed; snapshot/receipts cite source + run
Method: probe — read `ddl.ts:224-246`, `ledger.ts:28-37`, `facts.ts:101-110`, `atlas.ts:192-208`, `docs/routes/atlas.md` refusal paragraph
Result: better
Gate: irreversible
evidence:
- `lib/db/pglite/ddl.ts:224-246` kg tables: no `source`, no `ingest_run_id`
- `docs/routes/atlas.md` "`kg_node` / `kg_edge` have no `source` column and no `ingest_run_id`, so no join key runs to `ingest_run`" and "Scoring `kg_*` coverage is deliberately out of scope"
- `lib/analysis/atlas.ts:192-208` `INGESTED_SOURCES` — nine with `landing: "graph"`
- `lib/db/pglite/repositories/ledger.ts:28-37` `RUN_TABLES` = eight entity tables; `lib/testing/sentinel/facts.ts:101-110` same pinned list
- `lib/testing/sentinel/invariants.ts:372-417` uniformity exists only for `contribution_provenance`
- `docs/routes/data.md` snapshot `limits` carries `nodeKinds`/`edgeRels`, nothing per source
- `docs/routes/graf-permalink.md` "for `cesta`/`trasa` the sources still fall back to all four registries"
- `memory/kg-upsert-replaces-props.md`, `memory/loop-artifact-hygiene.md` (`persist-batch` refuses unregistered jsonb keys — the enforcement point already exists)

title: World time on the graph: valid_from/valid_to written, read, and joined to votes
body:
## Summary
The DDL declares world time on every kg claim and no writer populates it (`ddl.ts:288-290`); four features carry their own ad-hoc world time in props or in registry rows, so the product cannot answer "did the tie hold on the day of the vote" for the whole population.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 3 scout(s), theme T5 (World time on the graph: dated edges, role-window alignment, club-at-vote); deck rank #23 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

`lib/db/pglite/ddl.ts:288-290`: "valid_from / valid_to — WORLD time … Writers do not populate these yet (KgNodeRow/KgEdgeRow carry no world-time fields)". `lib/db/types.ts:174-202` confirms neither row type has them; `KG_EDGE_COLS`/`NODE_CONTENT` in `kg.ts:94-99` exclude them from the content tuple, so even a writer that set them would not trip the changed-content guard. Meanwhile world time leaks into props: `features/money/moneyLoader.ts:223` reads `props.role_valid_from`; `features/profile/careerSpine.ts:45,299` derives spans from `membership` rows; `features/denik/deriveDenik.ts:272,714` dates from its own `validFrom`; `memory/or-shareholder-entry-semantics.md` records that OR dates are registration dates, not acquisition dates — a semantics that belongs on the column, not in four readers. The DDL comment also collapses two states into one NULL ("unknown/unbounded"), which the missing-is-not-zero law forbids: "not known" and "still holds" are different facts.

Built: `validFrom`/`validTo` plus a `validity` tri-state (`known | open | unknown`) on `KgEdgeRow`/`KgNodeRow`; `mapKgEdge`/`mapKgNode` (`mappers.ts`) surface them; `supersedeUpsertChunk` includes them in the content tuple so a corrected date supersedes the old version; every writer that already knows a date (money ties from ARES VR `spolecnik[]` dates, `supplies` from contract signature, `belongs_to`/`influential_in` from `membership.from_at/to_at`, `sponsors` from tisk dates) writes it, and writers that don't write `unknown` — never a default. Then the cross-module payoff: a `kgNeighboursAt({ id, rels, worldTime })` read, and a deterministic "tie-at-vote" derivation in `lib/analysis/` that joins `linked_to`/`owns_stake` validity spans to `vote_event.voted_on` for all 207 MPs symmetrically, surfaced on `/poslanec` (money ties beside the votes they overlap) and `/volby` (which findings held during the term). Absence of overlap is a first-class finding.

## Flow
- Types + mappers + content tuples (`types.ts`, `mappers.ts`, `kg.ts`) — additive; existing rows read `unknown`.
- `lib/kg/prop-registry.json`: retire `role_valid_from`-style keys in favour of the columns; `persist-batch` refuses the old keys after a one-pass backfill (`kg-repair-*` precedent, replayable via `asOf`).
- Backfill pass per relation family, each with its own provenance stamp and ledger line; `guardKgReset` unchanged (no reset).
- `Store.kgNeighboursAt` + `asOf` combined read (record time × world time) with the same `warnIfTruncated` discipline.
- `lib/analysis/tieAtVote.ts` (deterministic, tested over fixtures): overlap spans → per-MP list of (vote, tie) pairs with the tie's `review_state` carried; `pending_review` never asserted as a conflict — it is a lead.
- Surfaces: `/poslanec` money section, `/volby` timeline, `/denik` dating from the column not the reader.

## Expected impact
Readers and newsrooms get the accountability triangle on a time axis for every MP, not a shortlist; measured by the share of `linked_to`/`owns_stake`/`supplies` edges with `validity != unknown` (0 % today) and by a new "ties overlapping ≥1 roll call" count on `/poslanec`. Could break: a registry date read as an acquisition date — the column must carry the semantics label (`registration` vs `event`) or the join lies.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the graph answers "connected WHEN", today only "connected"
Before: 0 kg rows with `valid_from` populated (DDL comment; no writer sets the columns; no mapper reads them); world time held in 4 feature-local shapes
After: per-relation coverage of world time reported on `/atlas` as a measured share; the tie-at-vote derivation runs over all 207 MPs
Method: probe - DDL, types, mappers, grep of `valid_from|validFrom` across features
Result: better
Gate: policy
evidence:
- `lib/db/pglite/ddl.ts:288-290,298-305` — world-time columns declared, "Writers do not populate these yet", NULL conflates unknown/unbounded
- `lib/db/types.ts:174-202` — `KgNodeRow`/`KgEdgeRow` without world-time fields
- `lib/db/pglite/repositories/kg.ts:94-99` — content tuples exclude `valid_*`
- `features/money/moneyLoader.ts:223` — `props.role_valid_from` (world time in props)
- `features/profile/careerSpine.ts:45,299`, `features/denik/deriveDenik.ts:272,714` — reader-local world time
- `memory/or-shareholder-entry-semantics.md` — registration-not-acquisition semantics currently held only in memory

title: Three money channels as dated graph edges (subsidy + donation join contracts)
body:
## Summary
Contracts are dated, directed, basis-tagged edges; subsidies and party donations are two undated scalars on the company node. Every surface that sums, gates or cites "reach" treats the three channels as one number, so two of the three cannot be dated, direction-checked, capped or cited.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 3 scout(s), theme T5 (World time on the graph: dated edges, role-window alignment, club-at-vote); deck rank #24 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

Today the money layer is asymmetric by construction. `lib/analysis/kg-money.ts:128` writes `supplies` edges with `signedOn` on the contract node and `direction`/`amountBasis`/`recipients_shared` on the edge (batch 014); `docs/data-analysis/graph-schema.md:42` records the company node carrying only `subsidies_total_czk` and `donated_to_party_czk` as props — no `subsidy` node, no `donates_to` edge. `mapLinkedToTie()` reads them straight off the node (`features/money/moneyLoader.ts:179-180`, `216-219`), and from there:
- `bucketReachCzk = contractCzk + subsidiesCzk` (`features/money/reachableMoney.ts:176`) adds a value that has no direction predicate (`moneyReachesCompany`, `:95`, runs on `supplies` only), no basis disclosure (`amountBasis.ts` counts contract rows only), no cap population and no per-grant citation. `moneyClaims.ts:116-144` mints `dosah-vazby` over that sum — a citable figure whose subsidy half cannot be re-derived at `/zdroj` below the company total.
- `/penize/strety`'s statute table fires `SUBSIDY_STATUTES` and `DONATION_STATUTES` on `subsidiesCount > 0` / `donatedToPartyCzk > 0` (`features/money/collisions/statuteRelevance.ts:38-51`), while gate 4 (`voteInRolePeriod`, `:80`) can only be day-precise for the vote — a grant drawn in 2012 makes a 2026 vote on 218/2000 a candidate exactly as a grant drawn last month does. The registry's temporal-alignment technique ("money flows are weighted by how much of them lands inside the window") is unimplementable for two of three channels.
- `docs/data-analysis/case-money/STATE.md` item 5: "SZIF subsidy channel absent from the corpus" — the largest Czech subsidy payer is not in the sum that the surface already labels as subsidies.
- `reviewSignal()` (`features/money/reviewTypes.ts:312-319`) lifts a tie for a "triangle" (contracts + subsidies + donation on one firm, `moneyLoader.ts:186`) — a compounding pattern the registry names, computed over one dated and two undated inputs.

Built: `subsidy:<source>:<id>` nodes (CEDR/DotInfo + SZIF open data, each with `amount`, `decidedOn`/`paidOn`, `provider`, `programme`, `amountBasis`) with `receives_subsidy` company→subsidy edges; `donation:<year>:<n>` or a direct `donates_to` company/person→party edge from the ÚDHPSH annual reports with `date`, `amount`, `donor_ico`. `kg-money.ts` gains two more pure builders beside `supplies`; `graph-schema.md` gains the rows; the supplies fold (`moneyLoader.ts:396-432`) becomes three channel folds sharing one `moneyReaches*` predicate family; `ReachableTie` carries per-channel `{czk, count, coverage}` and `reachableMoney` keeps the split; `MONEY_METRIC` gains `dotace-firmy` / `dary-firmy` so an aggregate claim is the sum of three citable sub-claims; `relevantStatutesFor` receives dated channel events and gates on the channel's date inside the role window, not on `count > 0`.

## Flow
- Write the schema + prop-registry rows (`lib/kg/prop-registry.json`, `graph-schema.md`) for `subsidy`, `donates_to`, `receives_subsidy`; add the pure builders in `kg-money.ts` with fixtures (no invented data).
- Ingest adapters in `lib/ingest/sources/` (CEDR/DotInfo, SZIF, ÚDHPSH), IČO-keyed only (`canonicalIco`), every record with source URL + accessedAt; persist via `persist-batch.ts` with a new pass; keep the legacy scalar props untouched until parity is measured.
- Parity gate: replay `subsidies_total_czk` from the new edges per company and report every company where the two differ; do not rewrite the scalar, disclose the delta on the company file.
- Refactor the fold: three memoized channel folds on `MONEY_MEMO_TTL_MS`; `CompanyContracts` → `CompanyChannel` × 3; `toReachableTie()` is the only constructor, so every caller receives the new shape by construction.
- Claims: extend `moneyClaims.ts` with per-channel metrics; `/zdroj` re-derives each; `/penize/[pspId]/paket` cites channel sub-totals.
- Strety: `relevantStatutesFor(tie, events)` takes dated channel events; `voteInRolePeriod` stays the one window test; coverage gains "grants inside window / total".
- Surfaces: ledger reach cell and the company headline print the three-way composition through one shared `ChannelDisclosure` (the `BasisDisclosure` pattern).

## Expected impact
Readers and journalists get a reach figure whose every koruna has a dated, directed, cited edge behind it; the review console sees which channel a lead rests on; strety stops manufacturing subsidy candidates from undated counts. Measured by: number of citable claims per tie (today 1 aggregate; after 3 + aggregate), strety candidate count before/after the date gate once ties are verified, and the parity delta table. What could break: the headline moves if Hlídač's subsidy totals disagree with the primary registers — the delta must be disclosed, never reconciled by repair.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - two of three money channels become dated, directed, citable facts instead of undated scalars
Before: 0 subsidy nodes / 0 donation edges in `graph-schema.md`; `bucketReachCzk` sums an undated `subsidiesCzk` into a figure minted as one claim (`moneyClaims.ts:116`); `SUBSIDY_STATUTES` gates on `subsidiesCount > 0` with no date (`statuteRelevance.ts:49`)
After: per-channel dated edges; strety subsidy relevance requires a grant date inside the role window; MISSING INSTRUMENT: a parity report new-edges-vs-`subsidies_total_czk` per company (does not exist yet)
Method: probe - read the writer, the fold, the claim minter and the statute table; confirmed no subsidy/donation node kind and no date on either channel
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
evidence:
- `docs/data-analysis/graph-schema.md:42-43` — company props `subsidies_total_czk`, `donated_to_party_czk`; contract node carries `signedOn`; no subsidy/donation kind.
- `lib/analysis/kg-money.ts:128` — `props: { amount, signedOn, supplierIco }` on the contract node only.
- `features/money/moneyLoader.ts:179-180, 186, 216-219` — subsidies/donations read as node scalars; `triangle` computed over them.
- `features/money/reachableMoney.ts:95-97, 176` — `moneyReachesCompany` is `supplies`-only; `bucketReachCzk` adds undated subsidies.
- `features/money/collisions/statuteRelevance.ts:38-51, 80-85` — count-gated relevance, day-precise window only for the vote.
- `features/money/reviewTypes.ts:312-319` — `reviewSignal` lifts on the triangle.
- `docs/data-analysis/case-money/STATE.md` open item 5 — "SZIF subsidy channel absent from the corpus".

title: Sealed graph passes with per-claim inclusion proofs
body:
## Summary
The ledger can seal an ingest run with a Merkle root, but nothing calls it, the derived graph (`kg_node`/`kg_edge`) is outside the sealable set, and no receipt can hand a reader a proof that the row it shows was in a sealed state — so the "tamper-evident" claim covers only the review chain.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 3 scout(s), theme T4 (Structured, sealed provenance per graph pass with a certified release); deck rank #25 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

`lib/db/pglite/repositories/ledger.ts:31-40` pins `RUN_TABLES` to the eight raw tables; `kg_node`/`kg_edge` — the tables every published number rests on (`docs/db-architecture-guide.md` accounting: 232 655 nodes / 371 137 edges) — are not sealable. `sealIngestRun` (ledger.ts:168-190) has zero production callers (grep over `scripts/`, `lib/ingest/`, `features/`: only the repository and its test), so `/data`'s "sealed runs" block (`features/data-releases/DataReleasesPage.tsx:447-462`) renders roots that exist only if someone sealed by hand. The pure primitives are complete and versioned (`lib/db/pglite/ledger.ts` — domain-separated leaf/node hashes, `merkleRoot`), but there is no inclusion-proof function and no table binding a root to a kg pass. The incident that makes this a moonshot rather than a nicety is in `memory/live-store-can-be-restored-under-you.md`: a stale backup replaced the live store, "no error anywhere; the surfaces kept rendering — just less", caught only by counting rendered blocks. A sealed root per pass turns that into a one-line check: recompute root(pass N) and compare.

Built: a `kg_seal` table (pass, track, root, leaf_count, sealed_at, writer ref) written by every graph writer at commit (`nextPass()` is already shared by all seven, `docs/routes/graph-writers.md`); a `merkleProof(leaves, index)` primitive beside `merkleRoot`; the receipt (`/zdroj`) and the evidence bundle (`app/graf/p/[ref]/bundle/route.ts`) carry `{ pass, root, leafHash, siblings[] }` so an auditor with only the published root verifies one edge without the store; `/data/manifest.json` and the `/dukazy` feed publish the roots; the sentinel (`lib/testing/sentinel/invariants.ts`) gains "recomputed root of the current serving graph equals the seal of its highest pass" — the restore-under-you detector.

## Flow
- `ledger.ts` (pure): `merkleProof` + `verifyMerkleProof`, same `politicas-merkle-*-v1` domains; leaf order pinned as `(src, rel, dst)` / `id` ascending (the listers' order, `kg.ts:250-268`).
- DDL: `kg_seal` (append-only, no updates), `disclosePendingDdl` reports it as additive; apply via `npm run db:migrate`.
- `LedgerRepository.sealKgPass(pass, track)` — hashes serving rows as served (mappers' output, not raw jsonb text, so key order cannot move the root); measure on the 2 GB copy and record the cost in `db-architecture-guide.md`.
- Every `da:*` writer seals after its transaction; `kg-repair-*` scripts included; the pass ledger line records the root.
- Receipt + bundle: proof for the cited claim at its current pass; `/overeni` verifies the proof locally before comparing values (a proof that fails is `unknown/zaznam-nenalezen`, never repaired).
- Sentinel invariant + `/data` root list from `kg_seal`; `sealIngestRun` finally called from `scripts/data-analysis/ingest.ts` on `finishIngestRun("ok")`.

## Expected impact
An external auditor (or the next concurrent session) can prove a claim was in pass N and detect a time-travelled store in seconds; measured as: seals per pass (0 today), proof-carrying receipts (0 today), and the sentinel's new invariant evaluated on every local run. Could break: a writer that forgets to seal leaves a pass unprovable — the sentinel must flag "highest pass in provenance > highest sealed pass" as a violation, not skip it.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - silent restores and partial wipes become detectable by hash, not by eyeballing counts
Before: `sealIngestRun` production callers = 0; sealable tables exclude kg_*; inclusion proofs = none; the 2026-08-05 restore was found by a manual render-count probe (59 → 27 blocks)
After: root per pass in `kg_seal`, proof per receipt, one sentinel invariant; the cost per seal recorded (MISSING INSTRUMENT today: hashing ~600 k rows has not been timed on this substrate)
Method: probe - repository grep for callers, ledger primitives, /data rendering
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence:
- `lib/db/pglite/repositories/ledger.ts:31-40` — `RUN_TABLES` without `kg_node`/`kg_edge`
- `lib/db/pglite/repositories/ledger.ts:168-190` — `sealIngestRun`; grep shows no caller outside the repo/tests
- `lib/db/pglite/ledger.ts` — `merkleLeafHash`, `merkleRoot`, no proof primitive
- `features/data-releases/DataReleasesPage.tsx:447-462` — roots rendered, nothing to verify against
- `app/graf/p/[ref]/bundle/route.ts` — the bundle a proof would ride in
- `memory/live-store-can-be-restored-under-you.md` — the incident
- `scripts/sentinel/run.ts:36-42` — invariants "the only thing standing between a formula correction and a silently stale published ranking"

title: Sentinel-certified releases: the verdict travels with the manifest hash
body:
## Summary
The sentinel is the only instrument that can see a stale ranking, and its verdict currently evaporates on stdout: `/data` stamps `latest` from cardinality floors alone, no surface shows when the invariants last held, and the hosted workflow is red by design with no cron.

## Description
Corroborated-by: 3 scout(s), theme T4 (Structured, sealed provenance per graph pass with a certified release); deck rank #26 of 47; full record docs/architect/moonshot-2026-09-01.md.

Today: `scripts/sentinel/run.ts:35-44` says it plainly — "Local `npm run sentinel` against a copy of the real store is the ONLY path on which the invariants actually execute"; `.github/workflows/sentinel.yml` has `workflow_dispatch` only, an ADOPTION POINT comment, and no schedule. The report (`lib/testing/sentinel/report.ts:65-76`) carries `manifestHash` but is written to an optional `SENTINEL_JSON` file and read by nobody: `getAdminData.ts` shows vault heads, ties, forensic and audit counts, never a sentinel verdict; `features/data-releases/manifest.ts` derives `latest`/`degraded` from `CARDINALITY_FLOORS` (`docs/routes/data.md` "Cardinality floors are a real gate") — floors that certified a 0,98 % contract corpus as `latest` for weeks. The 11-check roster (`invariants.ts:307-319`) covers only the contribution layer's provenance (`formula-ref`, `provenance-uniformity`, `components-sum`, `recompute-sample`); the money layer (`review_tier`/`review_rank` — memory: "153/208 ranks wrong after batch-012") and the law layer (`forensic_*` props, `amends` regen) have no invariant, so a half-applied money or law pass is exactly the "single-row generalization" the sentinel was built to catch, one module over. Degradations at the loader boundary — 121 `reportLoaderFailure()` call sites — go to `console.error` + a Sentry no-op (`lib/db/loaderGuard.ts:13-16`, no DSN in this repo), so "which surfaces fell back to mock in the last 24 h" is unanswerable; the architect backlog still lists "/admin ingest-status surfacing remains".

Built: (1) `npm run sentinel` persists its canonical report into a `sentinel_run` table keyed by `manifestHash` (or a JSONL sidecar like `driveLog` when the store is the thing under test — the copy is read-only, the live store gets the row on the next boot via `pending.ts`); (2) `deriveReleaseManifest` gains a `certification` field: `ok | violation | unevaluable | none` = the newest sentinel verdict FOR THIS manifestHash; `/data` prints "vydání latest, invarianty ověřeny k <date> (11/11)" or "neověřeno — sentinel nad tímto otiskem neběžel", and `/data/manifest.json` carries it; (3) the roster grows money and law lanes: `money-rank-cache` (stored `review_rank` == pure `reviewTier` for every tie, population shipped), `law-provenance-uniformity` (every bill verdict on one `{pass, ref}`), `amends-closure` (every `amends` edge resolves both ends and every bill with a verdict has ≥1 amends); (4) `reportLoaderFailure` additionally appends to a bounded in-process ring + JSONL (`.data/loader-failures.jsonl`) that `/admin` "Stav systému" renders as "degradace za 24 h: N (loader, count, last)" and the sentinel reads as a `loader-degradations` check (unevaluable when the file is absent, never ok); (5) the workflow ADOPTION POINT is wired to `npm run db:backup`'s pruned copy uploaded as an artifact from the ingest machine, so the nightly cron can return.

## Flow
- Add `sentinel_run(manifest_hash, ran_at, verdict, report jsonb)` to `CORE_DDL` via `db:migrate`; `scripts/sentinel/run.ts` writes it through a small `pending.ts`-style queue applied on next live open (the run itself never opens the live handle — keep that guarantee)
- `features/data-releases/manifest.ts`: `certification` derived from the newest `sentinel_run` row whose `manifest_hash` equals today's; `/data` §01 prints it; `loader.test.ts` pins page == `/data/manifest.json`
- Extend `SENTINEL_CHECK_LABELS`/`ORDER` with `money-rank-cache`, `law-provenance-uniformity`, `amends-closure`, `loader-degradations`; `facts.ts` collects the needed rows SELECT-only; the report schema stays `/1` (additive enum values only, per `report.ts:12-21`)
